When most people think of submarines these days, they probably recall the 2023 Titan disaster. The submersible vessel suffered a catastrophic implosion 3,500 meters below the surface of the Atlantic Ocean in its attempt to visit the husk of the Titanic, killing all five people on board.

The tragedy greatly diminished Americans’ interest in submersibles and actually fueled greater fear of traveling to the ocean’s dark depths, resulting in an inquiry by the U.S. Coast Guard and leading the exploration company OceanGate to shut down operations.

But pioneering ocean conservationist Dr. Sylvia Earle — the first person to walk untethered on the deep seafloor, who lived underwater for seven months on a research project — is trying to change that.

Her company DOER Marine, which designs underwater vehicles, has been working on a new class of submersible. The sub, named “Honu” after the Hawaiian word for turtle, will make its first dive in French Polynesia later this year, and can send three passengers 1,000 meters deep for eight hours at a time.

Earle firmly believes that going to great depths in a sub is "safer than flying" as long as companies are "certified by agencies who are in business to make sure you stay safe —unlike that little submersible that tragically didn’t come back from a trip to the Titanic."

open image in gallery Dr. Sylvia Earle has been a leader in ocean conservation for decades. She says it’s never too late to dive in ( Getty )

open image in gallery The Titan disaster is what many people think about when they think about underwater submersibles. Earle aims to change that with her new class of vehicles ( PA Media )

In a wide-ranging interview with The Independent, the 90-year-old deep-sea expert discussed her connection to the ocean and what humanity can do about threats to our health.

Earle made history as the first female chief scientist at the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration in 1990 and was one of the four women who lived underwater in the U.S. Virgin Islands Tektite II experiment in 1970.

But it all started on a beach in southern New Jersey. That’s where she first fell in love with the water, an obsession further fueled later on while diving in Florida.

“I first met the ocean when I was 3,” Earle recalled. “My parents had a family vacation on the Jersey Shore. And I remember first hearing the ocean, the waves crashing on the beach, and there was a certain smell that I had not noticed before.”

open image in gallery Sylvia Earle dives at Tetiaroa Atoll in French Polynesia. Earle has been spending time in the ocean since she was three years old ( Sylvia Earle )

She still dives in the Gulf of Mexico and offshore of the Flower Garden Banks National Marine Sanctuary near the Texas and Louisiana coastline.

There’s a coral reef there, teeming with life about 80 feet below the ocean’s surface.

Diving is something pretty much anyone can do, Earle said. Her mother waited until she was 81 to try it.

“So if you're 81, it's not too late. If you're 91, it's still not too late. If you're alive, it's not too late,” she explained. “And if getting into the water really isn't your thing, get into a submarine.”

open image in gallery A Honu submersible is seen underwater in this image from DOER Marine. The sub will make its first dive in French Polynesia later this year ( Sylvia Earle )

While there have been major strides in rocket technology that could one day transport humans to Mars and the farther reaches of the solar system, submersibles are the route to the largely unexplored deep ocean. Although more than 70 percent of the planet is made up of ocean, only .0001 percent of the deep ocean has ever been observed by scientists - leaving many mysteries to uncover about most of life on Earth.

That’s why conservation is so important, Earle stresses.

“The ocean is alive, but we humans have done our best to try to change that, to take life out of the ocean and market it, or to consume it, without understanding that the value of a fish alive greatly exceeds the value of a fish dead, now when half are already gone,” she said.

open image in gallery Whale watchers look out at the Pacific Ocean from Long Beach, California, in January 2016. Only .0001 percent of the deep ocean has ever been observed by scientists ( AFP/Getty )

Human greed has led to the loss of about half of coral reef ecosystems that support healthy oceans.

“It's just kind of disheartening to realize how one species — that would be us — how dreadfully effective we have been at eliminating the very fabric of life that is essential for our existence,” Earle said.

New threats continue to emerge each month. The Trump administration is moving to open up protected waters for deep-sea mining near American Samoa, weaken protections for Pacific marine monuments that support tourism and approve a $5 billion oil drilling project in the Gulf of Mexico.

open image in gallery Divers swim around a coral reef in Key West, Florida, in July 2023. The coral reef is the largest in the continental U.S. and helps to support marine life ( AFP/Getty )

Conservationists and environmental activists say that these actions will harm some of the most beloved marine species, like the humpback whale and green sea turtle, as well as those we rely on for food.

The ocean’s health is crucial for Earth’s survival. For one, oceans produce most of the oxygen we need to breathe. And oceans serve as a critical carbon sink, taking in much of the pollutants we release into the atmosphere that are warming our planet.

The energy industry has endangered that balance, Earle pointed out, with just 3 percent of the ocean safeguarded.

“We have been pushing the envelope. We are perilously close to tipping in the wrong direction,” she warned.

“But the good news is the kids are growing up knowing we've got problems. But they also know there are solutions and that on their watch, our watch right now, this is the best chance we have ever had as a species to shape the world we want, not just the world we get,” Earle added.

K-Pop Demon Hunters star Ejae has admitted she feels “haunted” by her performance at the Baftas earlier this year – claiming a poker-faced A-lister unwittingly put her off.

Ejae, Audrey Nuna and Rei Ami – who provided the singing voices for the HUNTR/X girl group in Netflix’s animated film – performed the movie’s hit track “Golden” for the star-studded audience at the London ceremony in February.

But Ejae, real name Kim Eun-jae, has now confessed that she wasn’t too pleased with her own vocals, telling The Times: “The Batas haunt me. I made mistakes. I cracked a little bit on the high notes.”

Explaining what happened, the 34-year-old continued: “Leonardo DiCaprio was [in the audience] right in front of me, and he was not smiling.”

Ejae added that as she was singing one of the song’s highest notes, she looked directly at the One Battle After Another actor.

open image in gallery It was the first time the trio were performing ‘Golden’ outside the US ( Bafta/YouTube )

“That’s what put me off,” she said. “He made me so nervous. It was already so nerve-racking to be in front of all these celebrities, and then I look up and lock eyes with Leonardo DiCaprio? Come on.”

Both the HUNTR/X singers and Titanic star DiCaprio were fixtures on the awards season circuit this year.

Released in 2025, K-Pop Demon Hunters fast became the most-watched film in Netflix’s history, amassing over 325 million official views, according to the streaming service. It followed up the astonishing viewing figures with plenty of accolades and Netflix has confirmed that a sequel is on the way.

open image in gallery DiCaprio at the Baftas ( Getty )

While K-Pop Demon Hunters was deemed ineligible for the Baftas because it wasn’t released in cinemas, it was named Best Animated Film at the Golden Globes, with “Golden” – co-written by Ejae – winning Best Original Song from a Motion Picture.

The film and its songwriters walked away with the same accolades at the Oscars, where Ejae also got a second chance at performing in front of Leo. That time around, things went a little better and the 51-year-old actor was even spotted waving a K-Pop lightstick as he stood to applaud.

DiCaprio’s star turn as Bob Ferguson in Paul Thomas Anderson’s acclaimed thriller One Battle After Another resulted in best actor nominations at all of this year’s major award ceremonies.

open image in gallery Ejae with her Academy Award ( AFP/Getty )

The actor didn’t manage to get his hands on any major statuettes, though, with Robert Arayamo (I Swear) pipping him to the post at the Baftas, before Michael B Jordan (Sinners) was victorious at the Oscars.

The Golden Globes splits its acting awards into Drama, and Musical or Comedy categories, with DiCaprio’s performance submitted in the latter. On the night, he lost out to Marty Supreme’s Timothée Chalamet.

News.title: ‘More pain’ to come after economic slowdown
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. The economy grew at a slower pace in the second quarter of the year, official figures show, under pressure from the Iran war.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc between April and June, down from 0.6pc in the first three months of the year, according to the Office for National Statistics.

The figures underline the challenge that the conflict poses for Andy Burnham, who has pledged to deliver “growth in every postcode”.

The Prime Minister has already been warned that the economy will slow further next year if Donald Trump continues his war in the Middle East.

Treasury officials have predicted UK growth of just 0.3pc in 2027 if the Strait of Hormuz stays blocked for the rest of this year.

That is far lower than the 1.6pc predicted by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) in March, based on assumptions made before the start of the war. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Iran war threatens to cripple growth, Treasury warns Burnham | Officials predict economic expansion of just 0.3pc in 2027 if Strait of Hormuz stays blocked

2) Britain facing £54bn bill for North Sea shutdown | Costs soar amid shortage of specialised ships needed to clear up abandoned oil rigs

3) Ban on zero-hours contracts to cost companies up to £3bn | Businesses face huge bill to offer workers guaranteed hours under Employment Rights Act

4) Nvidia’s AI push has echoes of Enron, says Big Short investor | Michael Burry claims chip giant is engaging in ‘circular’ financing

5) Shadow bank founder battles to stave off bankruptcy threat | Paresh Raja launches legal claim to prevent administrators from chasing him for repayment

What happened overnight

Asian shares were mostly higher, powered by gains for AI-related stocks including computer chips as regional markets tracked a rally on Wall Street.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 advanced 1.6pc to 68,601.21. In South Korea, the Kospi jumped 4pc, climbing to 6,844.65, as shares in Samsung Electronics surged 5.4pcc. Computer chipmaker SK Hynix jumped 7.1pc.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 0.3pc to 3,967.28, while the Shanghai Composite index added 0.5pc to 3,967.65.

In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.4pc to 9,155.80.

Data from the US on Wednesday showed consumer prices had risen in line with analysts’ expectations in July.

Wall Street stocks were boosted on Wednesday by gains made by tech companies CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer, both of which closed up by more than 19pc.

The Nasdaq Composite ended the session up 0.5pc, with the S&P 500 up nearly 0.3pc. The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished the session marginally down.

Oil prices were little changed as investors weighed the deadlock in talks between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, was broadly flat at nearly $89 a barrel.

News.title: H5N1 sparks a very Australian epidemic
News.content:
H5N1 bird flu has reached Australia’s shores and is threatening to infect some of the country’s most unique wildlife.

Australasia is the last continent to be hit by the highly infectious avian influenza H5N1, a new strain of which has been circulating worldwide since 2020.

Since recording its first case in June, more than 200 wild seabirds in Australia have been infected, with fears that the highly infectious flu could quickly ‘jump’ to other species.

While H5N1 has infected animals from foxes to sea lions in other parts of the world in recent years, the epidemic now threatens some of Australia’s most iconic wildlife – many of which are found nowhere else on earth.

An Australian government assessment of more than 2,000 native species warned that nearly one in five faces a high risk from the deadly H5N1 bird flu, with hundreds of unique birds and mammals vulnerable to severe population reductions or even extinction.

Those animals include iconic species like the Tasmanian devils, quolls, and dingoes.

Other aquatic mammals, including the platypus, which is only found in Australia, are at risk of infection through contact with bird droppings in shared wetlands and coastal environments.

News.title: Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

News.title: Advice, cookbooks and emergency pot noodles: Your best gifts for university students
News.content:
When it comes to sending a child or grandchild off to university, it can be tempting to fill their room with every conceivable gadget.

So to help, we asked the Telegraph Recommended Community for their best gift recommendations and their suggestions ranged from desk lamps to cookery books and supermarket gift cards.

Here are the essentials worth buying.

Kitchen basics

From cupboard essentials to electrical appliances and cookbooks, most readers say they’d gift kitchen equipment.

Thinking back to his university days, reader TJ, 43, from London, says “the main essentials are around kitchen items and good long lasting food”.

“It’s nice to have some bits to cook for others as well and to make friends quickly,” he adds.

Susan, 54, from the West Midlands, agrees, recommending “basic cooking equipment” as a key staple and “distinctive cutlery, plates and cups that are easily identified”, which are particularly useful for shared accommodation.

“A box of store cupboard ingredients such as olive oil, soy, stock cubes and spices to use when cooking,” is also well-received, she says.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check
News.content:
Newcastle 1 Everton 3

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

Sports.title: Premier League title winner tells Chelsea to raid Man Utd for ANDRE ONANA… despite goalie already making loan transfer
Sports.content:
QUINTON FORTUNE has told Chelsea to raid Manchester United for flop goalkeeper Andre Onana.

The stopper has already left Old Trafford this summer on a loan move to rejoin Turkish outfit Trabzonspor.



Onana, 30, spent last season on loan at the Super Lig outfit and made 33 appearances in all competitions.

The Cameroonian goalkeeper managed just six clean sheets and was unable to convince United of giving him another chance.



His move to Trabzonspor is a straight loan without an option to buy with his contract at United set to expire in June 2028.

Despite this, Fortune still believes that the former Ajax and Inter Milan star would be a useful addition to a club such as Chelsea.

Speaking to Premier Bet, he said: “Andre Onana could be an asset to Chelsea, Newcastle United or Aston Villa in the Premier League.

“You can see the quality for playing out from the back as many managers now want with their style of football, he can be your starting point.

“When you’ve got a goalkeeper like Onana who can ping a ball 50, 60 yards to your striker or midfielder and break the lines with his passes, that can make a huge difference, and he’s one of the best at it.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“He just needs to find his confidence again now because when a goalkeeper makes a mistake unfortunately the whole world sees it.



“I hope he can get back to his best because when you need a goalkeeper to play out from the back, he can be outstanding.”

If Chelsea were able to convince United into a deal which would see Onana’s loan cancelled then he would have to compete with Robert Sanchez for the no1 spot.

The Blues have already added experience to their ranks this summer with veterans Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson arriving.

Fortune earned a Premier League winners’ medal in 2003 as he helped Manchester United lift the title.

The former left-back admitted that he would have liked to have seen Welbeck return to Old Trafford.



However, for Chelsea, Fortune reckons new manager Xabi Alonso is doing well to bring leaders into the squad.

He added: “Xabi Alonso made some good signings for Chelsea this summer but I wish we could have seen Danny Welbeck return to Manchester United.

“By signing Welbeck and Jordan Henderson he wants to bring in some leaders to set good examples which you need at a club like Chelsea, especially after the experience Alonso had at Real Madrid.



“He’s looked at the Chelsea dressing room, felt that it was lacking something, and brought in the players with the right personalities and experience to make a difference in Henderson and Welbeck.

“They are not only top, top players but great professionals too.”

Sports.title: Stick to Football vs Rest is Football: How Lineker and Neville will lock horns in multi-million pound streaming war
Sports.content:
STICK TO FOOTBALL and The Rest is Football are set to battle it out in a multi-million pound streaming war this season.

Having each launched in 2023, both shows went from strength to strength during the World Cup.



Gary Lineker‘s The Rest is Football streamed daily on Netflix after securing an eye-watering £14million deal and performed well enough to earn a two-year extension up to Euro 2028.

Stick to Football, fronted by Gary Neville, also achieved huge numbers on YouTube during the tournament, landing itself a “multi-million pound” deal with Disney+ for the upcoming campaign in the process.



Jamie Carragher, a regular on Stick to Football, made a cheeky dig at his show’s rival after their initial Netflix deal was announced.

The former Liverpool star said: “The Netflix deal for the podcast that no-one listens to. I don’t know anyone who listens to it.”

Asked if it’s a true rivalry by The Athletic in June, however, Lineker ramped things up by saying: “Podcast-wise, no. We’re so far ahead in terms of the football.

“Theirs is a YouTube show and it does really well on YouTube — it’s not really a podcast. I saw Jamie last week and we had a bit of a laugh about it.”

Both shows feature star-studded panels.

Stick to Football is regularly co-hosted by Neville, Roy Keane and Ian Wright – with Jill Scott, Carragher and Wayne Rooney among their other regulars.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Rooney’s involvement will also increase next season, as a new “Stick to United” show is launched.

The Red Devils’ all-time leading goalscorer will team up with Mark Goldbridge for 50 episodes – which will also stream on Disney+.

The Rest is Football, meanwhile, features a more regular panel, with Lineker joined by Micah Richards and Alan Shearer.

During the World Cup they were joined by some star guests, however, including Man Utd star Harry Maguire.



Lineker’s show debuted on August 11, 2023 and has earned a not-to-be-sniffed-at 510,000 YouTube subscribers, despite the presenter himself calling it more of a podcast.

It was said to have reached 140,000 daily views on Netflix during the early days of the World Cup.

And last December Goalhanger, The Rest is Football’s parent company, claimed the show had a remarkable seven million monthly listeners.

Stick to Football, which debuted on September 27, 2023, also boasts huge listener numbers.

The Overlap, which is home to the show, has 1.75m YouTube subscribers.



And earlier this year they claimed to have 38m monthly views on YouTube.

A Disney+ premium subscription to watch the show on that platform costs £14.99 per month in the UK.

Netflix, meanwhile, is £18.99 per month for a premium membership.



Both shows have provided agenda-setting punditry.

And they have also ruffled some feathers.

In 2024, Keane sensationally compared Erling Haaland to a “League Two player” during an appearance on the show.

The comment reached then-Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola, who fired back: “I’m surprised this came from a former player. From journalists, I can understand, never been on the pitch but former players is always a surprise. It’s like the referees when they retire they criticise the referees.

“How difficult is that business for the players? It always surprises me. Their memory disappears quickly.



“The problems the players have, they had. They missed a thousand, million times and they were hurt when they were criticised by the former players.”

Lineker, meanwhile, got himself in hot water during Euro 2024 when he called England’s performance in a 1-1 draw with Denmark “s***”.

The comment led to skipper Harry Kane hitting back, saying: “What ex-players have to realise is that it is very hard not to listen to it now, especially for some players who are not used to it or who are new to the environment.

“I always feel like they have a responsibility. I know they have got to be honest and give their opinion but they also have a responsibility as an ex‑England player that a lot of players looked up to.

“People do care about what they say and people do listen to them.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Following post-World Cup breaks, both shows are set to return later this month.

And both, no doubt, will only further grow as agenda-setting football programmes.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes in horror penalty miss but laughs it off with Man Utd team-mates in Leeds friendly win
Sports.content:
BRUNO FERNANDES laughed off an embarrassing penalty miss in Manchester United’s friendly win over Leeds.

The return of the Premier League is just around the corner as the Red Devils continued their pre-season preparations on Wednesday.

Sports.title: ‘He’s a big old boy’ – Tyrone Mings backs wonderkid Brian Madjo, 17, to put 100kg frame to good use in Premier League
Sports.content:
TYRONE MINGS is backing teen star Brian Madjo to be a big hit for Aston Villa this season.

And given the striker weighs the best part of 100kg – or 15 and a half stone – it is hard to argue with that.



But Madjo showed in Villa’s Super Cup defeat to Paris Saint-Germain how he is much more than a classic target man.

The 17-year-old took his goal superbly in the 2-1 loss and already has people touting him as the successor to England captain Harry Kane.



Mings said: “Listen, obviously he is a tough person to defend against.

“I think he is about 100kg. He is a big old boy.



“But no, he has got a very high ceiling. He is very, very difficult to play against.

“And I just hope that he takes his goal and it fills him with confidence, and he can go on and contribute to the team.

“He said he was nervous, of course. He’s 17 and it’s a huge game.

“But I did say to him, ‘You get an amazing opportunity as a striker to just have one good moment and it can change everything for you’.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“I’m so glad that after missing a couple of chances, he got that goal.

“He’s a very humble lad. I think everybody wishes him all the very best and hopefully he can contribute in a big way for us on the pitch.”

Wednesday was Madjo’s debut for Villa and he caught the PSG defenders by surprise.

The teenager bullied the star centre-back pairing of Marquinhos and Willian Pacho, and another night could have had a hat-trick.



But former England defender Mings knows how tough it is to face Madjo – and Kane for that matter – as the teenager has been in training with Villa since January.

That was when the striker joined Unai Emery’s side from Metz, but registration issues halted his progress.

Fifa do not allow players under the age of 18 to move abroad, barring some exceptions like within the European Union, so they stopped Villa from playing Madjo after his £10million move from Metz.

The club eventually won an appeal via the Court of Arbitration for Sport earlier this month, citing how the striker was born in Enfield – despite having three caps for Luxembourg in friendlies.



Madjo has since represented England at Under-17 level and naturally social media has already anointed him as the Three Lions’ answer when Kane hangs up his boots.

And given the lack of top English strikers right now, the youngster should be eyeing the 2030 World Cup – and maybe even the home Euros two years before.

Mings added: “He is a good lad, great lad. He has obviously had to be very patient until he could play.

“So, I think that says a lot about his character. He is very young and very strong. Clearly, mentally he is able to deal with setbacks.



“He missed a few chances and scored probably the hardest of them all.

“But, yeah, a fantastic guy. I think you could see the reaction of everybody when he scored.

“It shows just how much he deserved it and that we were willing him to do well. I am delighted for him.

“He’s trained with us for a long time. So when he eventually got his chance to play, he was ready to play.

“He knew our system, he knew how to press. I presume he watched a lot of Ollie Watkins and understood how we play.”



Watkins missed the Super Cup after being given an extended break following the World Cup.

Madjo will compete with him for minutes this season and Mings thinks the England striker will be a great role model, too.

The Villa defender said: “I think the manager is big on what we do off the ball, probably more than what we do on the ball.

“Oli’s a great person to watch, because of his work-rate and what he brings to the team. He’s got Tammy [Abraham], too.

“That’s two very experienced strikers he has got in and around him. I’m sure he’ll learn a lot.”

Sports.title: Former Man Utd star and World Cup winner joins Zinedine Zidane’s new France set-up in shock selection
Sports.content:
FABIEN BARTHEZ has linked back up with old pal Zinedine Zidane after being handed a surprise role with France.

The former Manchester United keeper, 55, has been named as Les Bleus’ new goalkeeping coach.



France officially unveiled Zidane’s brand new backroom team on Thursday morning after he replaced Didier Deschamps in the top job.

And Barthez is one of the standout names joining the Real Madrid legend as France look ahead to Euro 2028 in England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.



The duo are by no means strangers, having been at the heart of France’s golden generation – winning the 1998 World Cup together before following it up with a Euro 2000 victory.

Since their retirement from professional football, their paths still seem to regularly cross at reunions for their 1998 side and charity games.

Barthez will now be tasked with looking after France’s keepers, taking over from Franck Raviot.

The shot-stopper – who earned 87 caps – became France’s undisputed No1 shortly after UEFA Euro 1996.

And it stayed that way until his international retirement in 2006.

His name is also remembered among Man Utd fans after Sir Alex Ferguson brought him to Old Trafford from Monaco in 2000.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Barthez spent four seasons at Old Trafford, making 139 appearances and lifting TWO Premier League titles.

Zidane has also turned to a familiar face in David Bettoni, who worked alongside him during both of his trophy-laden spells at Real Madrid from 2016 to 2018, and 2019 to 2021.

Hamidou Msaidie, Gregory Dupont, Stephane Plancque, Farid Tabet and Clement Ybert make up the rest of Zidane’s technical team.

Long-serving security chief Mohamed Sanhadji had raised some questions as to whether he would survive the shake-up.



Before the 2026 World Cup, the French Football Federation (FFF) advertised for a new head of security just days before the squad met up at Clairefontaine.

It was revealed that the former police commander – who has held the role since 2004 – received a donation from Kylian Mbappe in 2022, which he had declared.

But his FFF superiors thought it was irregular.

Nevertheless, then-boss Didier Deschamps stood his ground and made it clear they did not want to head to the US without him.

Reports suggest that Zidane is also keen to keep him around.



The France team will get their first taste of action together under Zidane when they travel to Turkey in the Nations League on September 25.

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard's call to Virgil van Dijk that saw Liverpool win Man City transfer battle
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard's call to Virgil van Dijk that saw Liverpool win Man City transfer battle

Virgil van Dijk was the subject of a transfer tug-of-war involving Liverpool and Manchester City with a phone call from Steven Gerrard proving key

View 2 Images Liverpool signed Virgil van Dijk despite interest from Man City

Steven Gerrard has recalled a phone call he received from Virgil van Dijk when he was being pursued by Liverpool and Manchester City where he delivered a blunt message to the defender.

‌



Van Dijk had established himself as one of the Premier League's best centre-halves and made it known to Southampton that he wanted to move on. A summer move failed to materialise, but the saga was always going to continue come January.

‌



Liverpool would win the race, spending a then club-record £75million to land Van Dijk, who made an instant impact as he helped the Reds make the Champions League final within months of joining.

‌



Gerrard recalls Van Dijk phoning him to so that he could get a greater impression of the Merseyside outfit. The Dutchman wasn't looking for the Liverpool legend to sell him the club, instead seeking a greater insight, but Gerrard did make it clear that Liverpool's traditions far exceeded City's.

The former midfielder recalled during Captains, a new LFC Original: “He phoned me at the time actually. I knew his agent really well. It was City, Liverpool.

“He said to me, ‘I haven’t phoned you to sort of push me one way or the other, because I know which way you’re going to push me. But just tell me a little bit about Liverpool?’

‌



“I just said to him, ‘Look, if it’s about what the clubs stand for and what the clubs are about, you’re wasting your time because I think you already know the answer to that.’ It was an interesting conversation and I was so happy that he chose us.”

View 2 Images Virgil van Dijk scored on debut for Liverpool back in 2018 (Image: Getty Images)

Van Dijk would enjoy the dream debut, scoring against Everton to knock them out of the FA Cup and concedes he was determined to wear red. “That feeling of, like, I wanted to play for this club so badly, it was so intense," he said. "And the fans embraced me from day one. Scoring also against Everton [on his debut] helped massively too!”

Article continues below

Within 18 months of signing Van Dijk had been named the PFA Player of the Year and proved crucial in Liverpool's Champions League success of 2019. The following year he helped the Reds' end their 30-year wait for a top flight title. Van Dijk remains Liverpool's defensive leader despite turning 35 this summer.

Sports.title: Liverpool 'pull out of transfer deal' for attacker after holding talks with agent
Sports.content:
Liverpool 'pull out of transfer deal' for attacker after holding talks with agent

Liverpool are pushing to bring in a winger before the window shuts on September 1 and had earmarked Bradley Barcola's PSG team‑mate Ibrahim Mbaye as a possible option

View 2 Images Liverpool have stepped away from pursuing a deal for Ibrahim Mbaye (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool have cooled their interest in Ibrahim Mbaye after discovering that a combined deal for him and Bradley Barcola could approach €200m (£171m). With the summer window ticking down, Liverpool are intent on signing at least one more winger.

‌



Mbaye, capable of operating on either flank, became PSG's youngest-ever starter at just 16-years-and six months, but his route to regular minutes remains blocked by Ousmane Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Desire Doue and Barcola. Liverpool's initial interest followed Mo Salah's departure earlier in the summer and continued uncertainty around Cody Gakpo ’s future.

‌



However, Fabrizio Romano reports that Liverpool have now stepped away from a potential move after holding talks with Mbaye's agent. Via his YouTube channel, it is claimed that Liverpool held talks with super agent Jorge Mendes over Mbaye, but PSG quoted the Reds around €200m for the pair.

‌



Liverpool could end up signing two new wingers for Andoni Iraola's squad, especially if Cody Gakpo joins Tottenham, but they believe that PSG's asking price for Mbaye is currently too high. Reports indicate PSG value Mbaye between €40m (£34m) and €50m (£42m).

Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola set to be handed new transfer priority as double update emerges READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool have already added one wide option this summer, bringing in Osasuna's Victor Munoz for £34m, but with Munoz operating on the left, the club still need a natural right‑sided winger to fill the long‑standing role previously held by Salah. Barcola, who was left out of Wednesday's UEFA Super Cup final against Aston Villa, remains an option as uncertainty over his future continues.

‌



PSG president Nasser bin Ghanim Al‑Khelaifi has also declined to rule out a potential departure, telling beIN SPORTS after the match: "We’re working calmly, we don’t talk too much, we do.

"I can’t say whether he will leave or not. Today, he is a PSG player. We’ll see!"

PSG boss Enrique sidestepped a question on Barcola's future, adding: "I don't know and I don't want to speak about any player individually because it's always dangerous when you are asking something positive or negative about a player. I stay focused on my team."

‌



View 2 Images It remains to be seen whether Liverpool will meet PSG's asking price for Bradley Barcola (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

Liverpool's chase has hit a major stumbling block, with PSG valuing the 23‑year‑old at around £145m - a fee that would eclipse the £125m Liverpool paid for Alexander Isak last summer. Romano adds that talks between the two clubs are still ongoing, with Barcola himself keen on making the move to Anfield.

With the window entering its final stretch, it remains unclear whether the Reds side will go anywhere near that price. Iraola made his need for a winger clear from the very start of pre‑season. "There are obvious situations where we need to sign players," he said.

‌



"Winger for example, we definitely need to sign a winger, but there are other situations where we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what is the cost, how we also see the players we have."

So far Iraola has welcomed Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo as well as Munoz.

Sports.title: Arsenal target's agent 'spotted' at Barcelona as Mikel Arteta stance emerges
Sports.content:
Arsenal target's agent 'spotted' at Barcelona as Mikel Arteta stance emerges

The agent of Barcelona defender Jules Kounde has been spotted at the club's training ground, with Arsenal reportedly among the clubs interested in signing the France international

The agent of Barcelona star Jules Kounde is reported to have been spotted at the training base of the La Liga club. The update comes amid fresh rumours that Arsenal have expressed an interest in signing the France international before the summer transfer window closes.

‌



Three new signings have been added to Arsenal’s squad that won the Premier League title last season, with Christos Tzolis, Illan Meslier and Bruno Guimaraes all moving to the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Arsenal have been linked with potentially strengthening their defensive options this summer, with Kounde, 27, mentioned as a potential target over the last few days.

The precise reason of the agent's visit to Barcelona's training ground remains unknown, though the timing has raised eyebrows and led many to speculate whether it is connected to the growing rumours surrounding a possible move to the Emirates.

It remains unclear what Arsenal's intentions are for the remainder of the summer transfer window, with speculation of a potential move for a new defender gathering pace amid doubts surrounding William Saliba's return.

Saliba picked up an injury during the World Cup with France and could face up to five months on the sidelines during his recovery, and may even require surgery. Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa is also being monitored.

Jurrien Timber, meanwhile, has been absent from all four of Arsenal's pre-season friendlies so far this summer, and travelled back to England from the club's training base in Spain earlier this month.

Article continues below

The Gunners have emphasised that this decision formed part of Timber's rehabilitation programme rather than a fresh injury setback.

Sports.title: Chelsea set Man City strict deadline to complete £120m Enzo Fernandez transfer
Sports.content:
Chelsea set Man City strict deadline to complete £120m Enzo Fernandez transfer

Chelsea have made it clear to Manchester City that they had to bid for Enzo Fernandez before the week is out if they want to have any chance of signing the midfielder

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez has been linked with a move away from Chelsea this summer (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

Manchester City have been told they need to submit a bid for Enzo Fernandez by 5pm on Friday - otherwise Chelsea will refuse to do business.

‌



City are among those keen on the Argentine midfielder, who has a good relationship with new boss Enzo Maresca, but the Blues want to avoid a saga that drags on until the end of the transfer window. The west Londoners want to ensure they know whether their player is sticking around, or could feasibly leave.

‌



They want new manager Xabi Alonso and his players to be able to focus on the new season ahead and Sky Sports reports that Chelsea insist any buyers have had two months to begin negotiations for Fernandez.

‌



Chelsea value Fernandez at £120m - meaning any move from City would need them to break their own transfer record for the second time this summer - and he has six years left on his contract.

Arsenal reignite Ezri Konsa transfer hopes but face massive Aston Villa problem READ MORE :

PSG chief drops transfer bombshell on Liverpool target Bradley Barcola READ MORE :

City's interest in Fernandez is closely linked to the future or Rodri. The Spanish World Cup winner has been at the Etihad since 2019 but Barcelona are keen and have seen a £40m bid rejected. The midfielder is keen to return home before his career is over and, should that happen this summer, City will need a replacement.

They have already landed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and remain in talks with Lille for Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, who enjoyed a stellar World Cup.

‌



Fernandez was dropped by Chelsea for two games in April after he admitted he would welcome living in Madrid, but Real Madrid themselves have moved to distance themselves from a move this summer. The player and his agent would later apologised for those comments.

View 2 Images New Man City Enzo Maresca has a good relationship with the Argentine

Relations with City and Chelsea have been stressed in recent months, owing largely to Maresca's move to Manchester. He admitted that he'd held talks with his new employers whilst he was still in charge at the Blues as the Etihad hierarchy looked to life beyond Pep Guardiola.

Article continues below

That saw Chelsea make the decision to axe Maresca in January and City eventually had to pay Chelsea £17m in compensation to appoint Maresca this summer.

Sports.title: PSG chief drops transfer bombshell on Liverpool target Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
PSG chief drops transfer bombshell on Liverpool target Bradley Barcola

Liverpool are still keen to sign Bradley Barcola and although Paris Saint-Germain's price tag is causing an issue, the French giants are officially open to selling him

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is top of Liverpool's shopping list (Image: FRANCK FIFE/AFP via Getty Images)

Paris Saint-Germain chairman Nasser Al-Khelaifi has refused to rule out selling Bradley Barcola in a boost to Liverpool's chances of signing him. Barcola, 23, remains the Reds' top target in the final knockings of the summer transfer window.

But negotiations have been at an impasse as PSG look to bank the maximum fee for the winger, who they value at an eye-watering £145million amid from Arsenal, too. Barcola was an unused substitute as Luis Enrique's side beat Aston Villa 2-1 to win the UEFA Super Cup in Salzburg on Wednesday, having only returned to training following the World Cup earlier this week.

Post-match, Al-Khelaifi was asked about the France international's future and couldn't give a definitive answer. "We're working calmly, we don't talk too much," Al-Khelaifi told Canal Plus.

"I can't say whether he will leave or not ... Today, he is a PSG player. We'll see."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The chairman's comments came after Enrique kept tight-lipped before the match. "I don't know and I don't want to speak about any player individually," the PSG boss stated.

"Because it's always dangerous when you are asking something positive or negative about a player. I stay focused on my team."

While the victory saw Barcola collect a fourth European medal in just over three years at PSG, the goals were scored by two players ahead of him in the pecking order. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia gave the Champions League holders an early lead before Villa equalised prior to half-time through Brian Madjo's strike. Desire Doue then restored PSG's advantage in the second half.

How much should Liverpool pay for Bradley Barcola? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola didn't feature against Aston Villa (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola also hasn't spoken about Barcola, although he his desire to sign a wide forward is no secret. "We definitely need to sign a winger," Iraola stated last month.

"But there are other situations where we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what is the cost, how we also see the players we have We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust, but it is still not the ideal situation, so it will depend on a lot of things."

Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Arsenal target 'favours' United as club stand firm on £14m star

Manchester United have time left to make further additions to their squad after already making significant additions in midfield

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has been building his squad for a new Manchester United season (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

The start of the new Premier League season is barely a week away and Manchester United have just one more match to go before the big kick-off. Michael Carrick will lead his team out against AC Milan - managed by his predecessor Ruben Amorim - in the final pre-season friendly for the Red Devils on Saturday.

‌



One week after that, Carrick's team will take on newly promoted Hull City in their Premier League opener. Last season's third-place finishers have already made additions to their squad but more could follow before the window shuts.

‌



Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have joined to bolster United's midfield, though Casemiro has left and Manuel Ugarte faces months on the sidelines with a knee injury. Other areas still need some attention and that's before we get onto the question of what's in store for Marcus Rashford.

‌



United have also built for the future with the addition of the likes of Tynan Thompson and another wonderkid could yet arrive. That's one area of attention today, along with the latest on a potential problem position.

Page won the Championship's Apprentice of the Year award last season, following in the footsteps of England internationals Jude Bellingham and Lewis Cook.

Sports.title: 7 transfer swaps that need to happen this window featuring Marcus Rashford and Viktor Gyokeres
Sports.content:
7 transfer swaps that need to happen this window featuring Marcus Rashford and Viktor Gyokeres

We've already seen one high-profile swap deal completed in the Premier League this summer

View 8 Images Brennan Johnson moved as part of an unusual Premier League swap deal (Image: Everton FC)

Premier League clubs are no strangers to the odd swap deal. And with less than three weeks remaining before the summer window slams shut, some sides could seek out trades.

‌



Whilst the concept of swapping one player for another in a mutually beneficial manner can often seem fanciful, these types of transfers do happen. Just this week, Everton sent Dwight McNeil to Crystal Palace for Brennan Johnson in a like-for-like swap.

‌



Ashley Cole for William Gallas, Alexis Sanchez for Henrikh Mkhitaryan, Zlatan Ibrahimovic for Samuel Eto'o. All of these player exchanges stick in the memory because of how they capture one's imagination. So why not take a look at some trades that could still be agreed upon before the window closes?

‌



From a blockbuster Arsenal and Manchester United switch to a Manchester City homecoming, Mirror Football takes a look at some, albeit very speculative, swap deals that should happen this summer.

Myles Lewis-Skelly and Marcus Rashford

The concept of a swap deal is akin to a video game and all of these suggestions should be taken with a pinch of salt. Many involve players who are either unlikely to leave or trades that teams probably wouldn't agree to.

View 8 Images Rashford could head to Arsenal if United want Lewis-Skelly

‌



But, in the case of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Marcus Rashford, the positives for both Arsenal and United are plain as day. With competition at left-back in the Gunners' locker room as strong as ever - Riccardo Calafiori, Piero Hincapie and Jurrien Timber are all capable - Lewis-Skelly was pushed into midfield last season.

He did play admirably, but Bruno Guimaraes' arrival at the Emirates will see his minutes further reduced and reports out of football.london claim he has been offered to both United and Chelsea.

Whilst other reports contradict this and state he is happy to stay, swapping him for Rashford would kill two birds with one stone. Arsenal need a skilful left-winger and Rashford, who wishes to leave Old Trafford this summer, fits the bill. Michael Carrick wants a left-back and Lewis-Skelly is young, homegrown and can help free up Rashford's wages. An admittedly unlikely win-win, no?

‌



Viktor Gyokeres and Julian Alvarez

If we continue to dip into the realms of the hypothetical, the Gunners' pursuit of Julian Alvarez could be eased by allowing Viktor Gyokeres to go in the opposite direction.

Since arriving from Sporting CP last summer for an initial £55m, Gyokeres has garnered mixed reviews but has become somewhat of a fan favourite. He scored 21 goals across all competitions last term, which is a pretty healthy return for a debut campaign.

View 8 Images Gyokeres can help Arsenal make an unlikely tilt for Alvarez

‌



But having won the Premier League title, the Gunners are looking to take the next step this summer. Their pursuit of Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Junior epitomises this.

Julian Alvarez is a name linked with an Arsenal move and Gyokeres could be used as a makeweight. The Atletico Madrid forward would cost upwards of £112m, so a fair chunk of money will have to be attached to the deal. But this way, the Spanish giants get their replacement and Arsenal get one of Europe's finest strikers.

Lucas Bergvall and Ferran Torres

As this summer began, Tottenham prodigy Lucas Bergvall made it clear he wanted to leave the club. Both Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes have been signed for a combined £185m in midfield and the young Swede evidently saw that increased competition would mean less playing time.

‌



View 8 Images Torres looks like he'll join PSG but Bergvall should aid a Spurs hijack

Since then, things have been ironed out with manager Roberto De Zerbi and the 20-year-old appears as though he'll stay. A £46m offer from Newcastle was supposedly turned down early in the window.

However, Spurs are on the hunt for a new winger and could perhaps use Bergvall to secure World Cup winner Ferran Torres. The Spaniard is reportedly PSG-bound, but with Barcelona holding a long-term interest in Bergvall, a swap deal proposal could put a halt to proceedings.

‌

Torres is valued at a similar £50m-plus mark to Bergvall and considering Barcelona's financial situation, they'd probably be keen on incomings that cost very little, if anything. Whilst it seems a near certainty he'll be joining PSG, Barcelona do like Bergvall and if things with him change, a last-minute hijack could be launched before Torres can put pen to paper with the Parisians to seal one of the biggest shock transfers of the window.

Omar Marmoush and Eric Garcia

Egyptian forward Omar Marmoush seems set to leave City this summer, with Pep Guardiola gone, Enzo Maresca installed and him plummeting down the attacking pecking order.

‌



View 8 Images Marmoush could be swapped for Garcia

John Stones has left the club and although they have plenty of options at centre-half, one more wouldn't hurt and again, Barcelona's financial struggles could be capitalised on. Eric Garcia actually progressed through City's youth system before leaving for free in 2021 and he has become a solid deputy for Barcelona.

A player like Marmoush, however, would help them fill a gap up front and the 25-year-old Garcia's homecoming would bolster City's backline. A small fee may have to be included on Barcelona's side as Marmoush is worth a fair deal more, but this swap would no doubt strengthen both sides.

‌



Joshua Zirkzee and Alex Valle

It is no secret that Joshua Zirkzee wants to leave United this summer and Italy looks to be his likely destination, with Juventus, Roma and Como all reported suitors.

Should Cesc Fabregas' Como be a preferred landing spot, then United could opt to end their left-back search by requesting young defender Alex Valle be included in the Zirkzee deal. The Dutch striker is valued at a reported £20m and Valle would come in at slightly less, so cash would be necessary.

View 8 Images United want to offload Zirkzee and sign a left-back

‌



But with this swap, Como get a forward who thrived the last time he played in Serie A and would be eager to rediscover form. And United get a possible future replacement for Luke Shaw without breaking the bank at all. Valle is a promising young Spanish left-back who made 28 league appearances for Como last season, helping them qualify for the Champions League.

Marc Guiu and Lewis Dunk

Chelsea have torn their transfer policy to pieces this summer and instead of targeting unproven, up-and-coming talent, have secured stars steeped in Premier League experience. Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson have both arrived.

View 8 Images Chelsea and Brighton have a good relationship when it comes to transfers

‌



Striker Marc Guiu, who spent last season on loan at Sunderland, is expected to leave the Blues this window and is valued at around £20m. So, with Trevoh Chalobah leaving and a defensive leader something Xabi Alonso's side could do with signing, why not make a move for Lewis Dunk?

He suits Alonso's system like a glove and if Chelsea want an experienced defender to bring off the bench, the 34-year-old is unrivalled. Dunk is keen to be a one-man club and stay at Brighton, but could be tempted by one last hurrah at the top table. Not to mention, these clubs have a breadth of transfer history, with Moises Caicedo, Marc Cucurella and others moving between them.

Brighton could do with attacking reinforcements, having given up Welbeck to Chelsea, and the arrival of Luka Vuskovic means losing Dunk would not be a disaster. Whilst this swap deal is the stuff of fantasy, it would provide the Seagulls with a raw, young striker of the future and Chelsea with a defensive general suited to their ball-playing, possession-based system.

‌



Gabriel Jesus and Amir Rrahmani

William Saliba's injury means that Arsenal are set to start the season thin at centre-half, with Cristhian Mosquera the likely partner to Gabriel. But should either get sidelined, Arteta could be left in a bind and so Gabriel Jesus could be used in a swap deal for a new centre-back.

It seems as though the Brazilian striker will join Napoli, having fallen out of favour behind Gyokeres and Kai Havertz in north London. A £17m deal has been mooted, but why not instead tempt the Italian outfit to part with Amir Rrahmani?

View 8 Images Jesus is all set to join Napoli

Article continues below

Fans of English football may not be familiar with the 32-year-old Kosovan captain, but Rrahmani has been crucial to Napoli's recent successes, helping them to the Serie A title in 2022/23. He boasts elite passing ability and exceptional aerial dominance that the Gunners would be lacking without Saliba.

Rrahmani isn't exactly best suited to a high line and could be found out in a front-footed defence, but swapping him for Jesus plugs the Saliba gap and brings in a proven winner. Convincing Napoli to part with him would be the toughest part of this speculatively suggested swap deal, however.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta eyes Barcelona raid as £85m star opens door to transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta eyes Barcelona raid as £85m star opens door to transfer

Mikel Arteta is eager to improve his Arsenal squad ahead of the new Premier League season

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta continues plotting Arsenal's next move in the transfer market (Image: Carlos Jasso/AFP)

Mikel Arteta remains focused on bolstering his Arsenal squad before the summer transfer window closes. The Premier League champions begin their title defence in eight days against Coventry City, but first face Manchester City on Sunday in the Community Shield.

‌



Despite missing out on Vinicius Junior after he signed a contract extension with Real Madrid, the Gunners acquired his international team-mate Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United in a £75million deal.

‌



The 28-year-old's arrival marked Arsenal's fourth summer signing, but plans to add further remain among Arteta's priorities. The north London side are said to be targeting a Barcelona star, while an £85m-rated player has opened the door to an England move.

‌



Barcelona target emerges

Arsenal have attempted to sign defensive reinforcements this summer, but to no avail. William Saliba's absence for "an extended period" leaves Arteta without one of his best defenders ahead of the new season.

The Premier League champions have been interested in Aston Villa star Ezri Konsa but are set to turn their attention to Barcelona defender Jules Kounde, if the France international opens the door to a possible move, Spanish outlet Sport reports.

Tottenham could hand Arsenal major transfer boost after opening Folarin Balogun talks READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The outlet claims that Arsenal are looking for a centre-back, who can also cover the right side of defence. Kounde, 27, certainly fits the bill as prior to joining Barcelona, he played in central defence for Sevilla and moved to full-back after signing for the Catalan giants, which is a position he also plays for the national team.

Kounde is said to be a cheaper alternative to Konsa, who has been valued at £60million by the Europa League champions. The Frenchman has reported for pre-season training in Spain and played a key role in Barca's back-to-back title triumphs.

View 3 Images Jules Kounde is reportedly a target for Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



£85m star open to Premier League move

Bayer Leverkusen star Christian Kofane revealed that he'd be open to joining the Premier League in the future. The 20-year-old impressed in his debut season with the Bundesliga club, with seven goals and nine assists in 44 games.

The striker came up against the Gunners last season in the Champions League round of 16 and showcased his potential in both legs despite his side coming up short. His agent Eric Depolo seemingly claimed that his performances led to the Gunners enquiring about his situation, but warned them that they'd have to part ways with £85m to get his client.

He told Daily Arsenal earlier this year: "Yes, Arsenal's interest is genuine. The manager [Mikel Arteta] likes him very much. I think it is too early to say [which club is leading the race].

‌



View 3 Images Christian Kofane has been linked with a move to Arsenal since last season (Image: Getty Images)

"But due to the fact that the player speaks Spanish, like Mikel Arteta, and that William Saliba is originally from Cameroon, I would say Arsenal are in pole position."

Depolo added: "He is a €100million (£85m) player. With Kofane, Arsenal will have a top striker for the next 10 years." Opening up about a possible move to England, Kofane told Kicker: "I can certainly imagine it, yes.

Sports.title: Australia exposed by Bangladesh in stunning start to first Test
Sports.content:
Bangladesh's bowlers overshadowed Australia's Big Four getting back together on day one of the first Test as the host was dismissed for 198 and Hasan Mahmud took a career-best 6-55.

Bangladesh's top-order batters then combined to reach 96-1 at stumps and cut the first-innings deficit to 102.

Bangladesh lost their last Test match against Zimbabwe in June by an innings and 85 runs but in Darwin on Thursday made a dream start to their tour of Australia, where they are playing their first Test series since 2003.

Australia are beginning a schedule of at least 20 Tests over the coming 12 months, with tours of New Zealand, South Africa, India and England - where The Ashes begins at Trent Bridge from June 18. Steve Smith admitted their start against Bangladesh was "not our best"

"Still plenty of cricket to be played, obviously," Smith added.

"It would have been nice to have taken a few more [wickets]. So, hopefully we start ⁠well in the morning, pick up a few early ones and ⁠put pressure on."

Mahmud starred for the visitors with consistent line and length, striking in his sixth and seventh overs to remove openers Jake Weatherald (23) and Travis Head (22) after Australia won the toss and raced to 45 without loss on a green-tinged pitch.

Image: Bangladesh's Hasan Mahmud made the difference with the ball on day one

From there, Mahmud and fellow pacemen Taskin Ahmed (2-55) and Ebadot Hossain (2-39) dominated the first two sessions, bowling with discipline to exploit the conditions and get on top of a batting line-up that was held together primarily by Smith's defiant 71.

Smith was the next-to-last wicket to fall, advancing at Mahmud before top-edging a high catch to wicketkeeper Litton Das, bringing an innings featuring seven boundaries and a six to an end.

The day started positively for the hosts, with skipper Pat Cummins winning the toss. Playing just his second Test in 13 months, he reunited with fellow pacemen Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc and veteran off-spinner Nathan Lyon in a frontline attack long known in Australia as the Big Four.

A partisan crowd was in full support of Darwin-born Weatherald but he never really settled and needlessly swiped at a ball from Mahmud. Head was out soon after, chopping on a delivery that was bowled from around the wicket as Australia slipped to 52-2.

Ebadot had Marnus Labuschagne (1) caught by Bangladesh skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto, and could have dismissed Smith early too, but a chance at third slip was put down.

Sports.title: Could UK diaspora players represent India? | Bhatia closes in on Liverpool stake
Sports.content:
Welcome to Dev's Digest, a regular Sky Sports column in which Asian Football Award winner Dev Trehan delivers exclusive news and reflects on some of the key developments for British South Asians in Football.

Indian football chiefs are increasingly confident that diaspora footballers from Britain will be allowed to play for the national team, Sky Sports News can exclusively reveal.

Current rules prevent Indian-heritage footballers abroad from playing for the national side unless they surrender their overseas passport.

That has prevented British Indians from earning international recognition and the opportunity to help India break back into the world's top 100 FIFA-ranked nations.

But one senior official has told Sky Sports News he is "convinced" the path will be cleared to allow eligible overseas footballers to represent India.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After the All India Football Federation set up a task force to assess the status of players of Indian origin who could represent the national team, Arunava Chaudhuri told Sky Sports News’ Dev Trehan he thinks four or five British Indian lads could get into the squad

Reacting exclusively to Sky Sports News, former Mumbai City FC chief operating officer Arunava Chaudhuri said: "We are closer than we've ever been to seeing Overseas Citizens of India representing the Blue Tigers.

"Diaspora footballers from Europe can take the Indian team to another level.

"We're now talking about something that potentially extends beyond football, with the next Commonwealth Games coming to Ahmedabad, and their bid for the 2036 Olympic Games."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch some of Michael Chopra’s best goals for clubs including Newcastle, Sunderland and Cardiff City

Sky Sports News has followed the story of Indian-origin British footballers trying to play for India for more than a decade.

In 2014, former Newcastle striker Michael Chopra told Sky Sports News he was ready to play for India and that cricket great Sachin Tendulkar was ready to help him fulfil that desire.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former Wolves' capain Danny Batth is half-Indian and told Sky Sports News in 2017 that would love to play for India

In 2017, Danny Batth, who has just signed for Millwall and whose father was in born in Punjab, told Sky Sports News senior correspondent Rob Dorsett about his desire to play for India.

West Ham chief Virani targets Premier League return

West Ham interim chief executive officer Karim Virani wants the club to continue driving positive change, but admits the main goal is to make an immediate return to the Premier League.

The Hammers beat Leeds United in their final game last season, but it wasn't enough to prevent them from finishing 18th and suffering relegation.

"As we look ahead to the new [league] season, it's less than a week now and we have our first match, which has come around incredibly quickly," Virani said.

"The strength of the West Ham family in terms of supporting our team is going to be so crucial to our objectives as a football club - and everyone is aware we have one primary objective this year, which is to get out of the Championship and back to the Premier League.

Image: West Ham CEO Karim Virani in conversation with Sky Sports News' Dev Trehan (Photo: Vijay Bedesha)

"While it becomes very easy to quickly focus on the football, we should never forget the responsibility we have as a football club to drive positive action and impact off the pitch too.

"Personally I'm incredibly passionate about West Ham being at the forefront of championing equality and celebrating inclusion, and ensuring all of our matches - men's, women's and academy - are environments where everyone feels welcome."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kevin Nolan and Darren Moore tell the EFL show why Jarrod Bowen is key for West Ham's hopes for an instant return to the Premier League.

Virani was speaking at a West Ham United and Inclusive Irons event with Desi Ballers to close South Asian Heritage Month.

The event - also attended by club ambassadors Matt Jarvis and Bobby Seagull - shone a light on West Ham's work in the community.

We often hear about dream debuts in football, but it's fair to say Yan Dhanda's first appearance for Swansea - and indeed his first taste of senior professional senior football - was exactly the stuff that dreams are made of.

It was a sunny afternoon at Brammall Lane, with the game locked at 1-1 in the closing stages of Graham Potter's first game as Swansea boss, away at Sheffield United.

"It was crazy. I'd done really well in pre-season. I was only 19 but I was confident. I wanted to play. We got to Sheffield and I knew I was on the bench," Dhanda told me for Sky Sports News in 2018.

"I went to sleep and kept waking up. It was the first time I've ever been in a pro game. All I could think was coming on and scoring.

"Come the game, I was on the bench for the first time in a professional game. It's the Championship, I'm sitting there thinking this is fast, this is harder than I thought.

"It was late in the game when Graham Potter told me I was coming on and I was buzzing - 30 seconds later, the ball fell to me in a good position where I backed myself.

"I just hit it and then it was a mad blur. My dad and cousin were in the stands right behind that goal. It was honestly the best feeling."

Sports.title: O'Hara: Spurs should sign Rashford with De Zerbi 'perfect' for him
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham midfielder Jamie O'Hara wants Spurs to sign Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford.

Speaking on Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast, O'Hara believes Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi is the "perfect man-manager" for Rashford, whose Man Utd future remains uncertain.

Sky Sports News understands a new left-sided forward is a priority for Tottenham amid interest in Manchester City's Savinho and Liverpool's Cody Gakpo.
