World.title: More and More Filipinos Are Working in Croatia
World.content:
August the 12th, 2026 – More and more Filipinos are being registered as living and working in Croatia, with the vast majority employed in the tourism and trade sectors.

As Jadranka Dozan/Poslovni reports, over the first seven months of this year, a total of 106,400 permits were issued to citizens of third countries (countries outside of the EEA), of which almost two-thirds were for work in tourism and construction.

The number of issued work permits is reportedly falling, but Interior Ministry data doesn’t show the real number of workers from abroad. The latest data from the Ministry of the Interior on permits issued to foreign workers from so-called third countries only confirmed the continuation of the year-on-year decline in their overall number. This is partly a consequence of the fact that since March last year the maximum duration of permits has been extended from one to three years.

this “decline” isn’t straightforward

How much of this alleged decline is explained by that change in legal rules, and how much is contributed by generally tightened rules or some other reasons (such as meeting part of the need for workers through increased work engagement of domestic pensioners or, for example, returnees to Croatia), the Interior Ministry statistics don’t reveal.

In the first seven months of 2026, a total of 106,400 residence and work permits were issued to citizens of “third countries”, which is 7.5 percent less than last year. Looking only at July, almost 23 percent fewer were issued than last year.

seasonal employment

So far in 2026, the share of permits for seasonal jobs increased significantly, they’re actually up by 40 percent compared to last year – while those for new employment are down 31 percent, and permit extensions are up around 10 percent. Looking only at the month of July, Interior Ministry data reveals that a total of 12,282 positive decisions were issued for imported labour (compared to 15,905 in the same month last year). Almost every fourth of these, or more than 3,000 permits, was given for seasonal work, while just over 9,000 relate to new employment (just under 4,500) and permit extensions (just under 4,800).

40 percent is how much the number of permits for seasonal jobs has risen this year compared to last year, and it’s far from insignificant. Looking at the situation by activity, almost two-thirds of permits go to the two sectors where the import of workers is normally the most massive, tourism and hospitality, as well as construction. This applies both to those issued last month and to the total number issued since the beginning of the year. However, in construction there are 17 percent fewer this year than in the first seven months of last year, while in tourism and hospitality activities there are 5.4 percent more.

Of the other three most represented sectors when it comes to importing workers, an increase in the number of issued permits in 2026 is recorded only in trade. This also contributes to changes in the structure of issued permits in terms of the origin of workers. By far the largest growth is recorded for those issued to Filipinos – almost 50 percent higher than last year. Filipino workers, in addition to the tourism sector, are most often engaged by employers from the trade sector.

misleading statistics

The Interior Ministry’s records of work permits, however, fail to reveal many things and are certainly not the best indicator of the real situation regarding how many workers from third countries there are in Croatia. Experts on migration and demography have been pointing out the problem of recording foreign workers in general for a long time.

On the occasion of the recent publication of data by the Croatian Bureau of Statistics on migration for 2025, one of the more active among them, Tado Jurić, once again warned about the methodological challenges in this area. From the official data of the Interior Ministry and the CBS (according to which 56,700 immigrated foreign citizens were recorded last year), no one can say with certainty how many of them are actually in Croatia because these are records of different phenomena, he says.

For that reason, the number of insured persons in the Croatian Pension Insurance Institute (HZMO) is usually considered a somewhat more authoritative indicator. In its records in the middle of this year there were a little under 151,000 insured persons who are citizens of third countries (more precisely, with travel documents of those countries), which is about 29,000 more than at the end of last year. Although these are insured persons (which does not automatically mean employees), this is still roughly the indicator closest to reality, and it roughly implies that every 12th person who works and/or pays contributions in Croatia is a foreigner.

“practically half of croatia’s foreign workforce comes from africa and asia”

Given that practically half of the foreign workforce in Croatia today comes from Asia and Africa, migration experts have long emphasised that this requires active management of the processes, both in the context of integration and policies aimed at stronger activation of one’s own potentials. Due to low labour productivity in the public sector, it is often pointed out that there are certain employment reserves there for the entrepreneurial sector, but reforms of that kind do not come easily.

World.title: Almost All Istrian Beaches Have Excellent Quality Seawater
World.content:
August the 12th, 2026 – Almost all Istrian beaches have excellent quality seawater according to the latest measurements, with only four lagging behind.

The sea at Istrian beaches continues to be of exceptionally high quality. In the sixth examination of this year, conducted from the 28th of July to the 6th of August, as many as 98.2 percent of the seawater samples received an excellent rating. Index reports that the sea was sampled at a total of 222 measuring points on beaches from Savudrija to Brestova.

During the process of seawater sampling, the sea temperature ranged between 24 and 29 degrees, while the air temperature was from 24 to 33 degrees.

only four locations were less than exceptional

Excellent swimming seawater quality was recorded at 218 measuring points. Good quality was also recorded at one location, in Ližnjan at Matićev Pisk below the hotel. At three locations, the sea received a satisfactory rating only. These are AC Kažela – FKK in Medulin, Tarska vala in the Tar-Vabriga area, and the location near Hotel Molindrio in Poreč.

bacteria measuring

When examining the seawater, the quantities of intestinal enterococci and the bacterium Escherichia coli are determined as indicators of microbiological pollution. During the sampling process, meteorological conditions, sea temperature and salinity, as well as any visible pollution, are also recorded.

Based on the results of individual samples, the sea is classified as excellent, good or satisfactory. The results of all individual examinations are available via the online application of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Green Transition.

World.title: Economy minister rejects proposed restrictions on nicotine products
World.content:
Economy Minister Erkki Keldo declined to approve a draft bill aimed at curbing the use of nicotine products among young people as the proposed changes could have a significant impact on sellers and importers.

The restrictions proposed by the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Ministry of Justice would allow nicotine pouches, nicotine strips and nicotine sprays containing no more than four milligrams of nicotine per gram to be sold in Estonia. The aim is to reduce the use of nicotine products among young people.

Erkki Keldo sent a letter to the Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs on Wednesday informing it that he had declined to approve the draft bill. Keldo said the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications supports protecting the health of children and young people and curbing the illegal sale of nicotine products, but considers it important that measures restricting freedom of enterprise be sufficiently justified and proportionate.

Snus. Source: Flickr

"The changes proposed in the draft bill could significantly affect manufacturers, importers, wholesalers and retailers of nicotine products operating in Estonia. The explanatory memorandum does not adequately assess the extent of these impacts or provide a convincing justification for the proposed maximum nicotine content of 4 mg/g for nicotine-containing products related to tobacco products," Keldo said.

He noted that the draft bill's maximum nicotine content of four milligrams per gram is based on Latvia's approach, but said this was not sufficient justification for restricting freedom of enterprise.

"The explanatory memorandum does not indicate the nicotine content of nicotine pouches and other products covered by the bill currently on the Estonian market, what proportion of products currently marketed legally would comply with the proposed limit or how many businesses and products would be affected by the change," the economy minister said.

He is also dissatisfied that the draft bill does not include a comparative analysis of approaches taken by other EU member states or explain why Latvia's regulations are the best model for Estonia.

Keldo said the explanatory memorandum needs to be supplemented with a comparison of different options. The impact of the limit on the health of children and young people, the risk of accidental poisoning, businesses, the functioning of the legal market and consumer behavior should also be analyzed.

The data presented in the explanatory memorandum concern products containing e-cigarette liquid, but does not address the impact of the changes on nicotine pouches, strips, sprays and heated nicotine sticks.

"We ask that the impact assessment be expanded to separately cover all product categories regulated by the draft bill and the requirements proposed for them," the minister said.

Keldo also wants the impact of the changes on Estonian manufacturers, exports, employment and regional businesses to be examined, along with their impact on the legal market, illegal trade and tax revenue.

"Possible substitution behavior must also be analyzed, including whether some consumers could switch to products with unregulated contents or to other tobacco and nicotine products and what impact this could have on achieving the draft bill's public health objective," Keldo said.

The Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications is also dissatisfied with a provision in the draft bill stipulating that products may not contain substances that produce a flavor or aroma other than tobacco or menthol and that only substances listed in a specific regulation may be used to provide those flavors. However, the explanatory memorandum does not explain why those particular substances are considered suitable or what costs businesses could incur in reformulating existing products.

Keldo said the bill's relationship with the planned update of the European Union's legal framework for tobacco and nicotine products should also be assessed.

The Ministry of Social Affairs has previously said that people are starting to use nicotine products at increasingly younger ages. While young people previously tried nicotine at ages 15 or 16, they are now doing so at around age 11. Nicotine pouches and e-cigarettes are the most common products used by those starting out.

Estonia's so-called Superministry building housing several government ministries. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Just over one-fifth of the nicotine products currently on the market comply with the requirements proposed in the draft bill. Around 60 percent of products would have to be reformulated, while nearly one-fifth would have to be removed from the market.

Several European countries have tightened restrictions on nicotine products in recent years. Latvia raised the minimum age for purchasing tobacco and nicotine products to 20 two years ago. No such proposal is currently under consideration in Estonia.

The new rules are planned to take effect in 2028, although the exact date will be determined as the draft bill moves through the legislative process.

World.title: Baltics' first AI factory to open in Estonia
World.content:
Dutch cloud company Nebius' Tallinn AI factory will begin operating at Greenergy Data Centers' data center this year. With a capacity of 22 megawatts, it will be the largest in the Baltics.

Nasdaq-listed Nebius announced Wednesday that it signed agreements in the second quarter to expand the company's AI infrastructure network in Europe. The first phase of its Tallinn AI factory, with a capacity of 22 megawatts, is expected to begin operating later this year.

Nebius Head of Communications Tom Blackwell said Estonia was a natural choice for the company thanks to its world-class engineers, vibrant digital economy and startup culture, as well as its ambitious plans for both artificial intelligence and the transition to clean energy.

"Nebius' Tallinn AI factory, which is being developed in partnership with Greenergy Data Centers, will provide state-of-the-art infrastructure to support Estonia's growing innovation ecosystem and help accelerate the development and adoption of artificial intelligence," he said.

Nebius' global capacity network has expanded rapidly. In Europe, the company is developing large-scale AI factories in Lappeenranta, Finland, and Béthune, France. It also has an operating center in Mäntsälä, Finland, as well as AI infrastructure projects in the United Kingdom, Spain and Iceland. Nebius' major customers include Microsoft and Meta.

Greenergy Data Centers CEO Kert Evert said Nebius' decision to choose Greenergy shows that Estonia is emerging as a competitive destination for large-scale AI infrastructure projects.

Blackwell said Nebius wants to work closely with the Estonian government, businesses and universities to develop AI skills, broaden access to artificial intelligence capabilities and strengthen Estonia's position as a leading hub for AI innovation.

Martin Salo, co-founder of Tensor Estate, a group of Estonian entrepreneurs that became a shareholder in Greenergy Data Centers last month, said the newly announced project is the first phase of a larger development that will make Estonia one of the international hubs for AI infrastructure in the coming years.

"Until now, Northern Europe's major AI factories have been concentrated primarily in Finland, Sweden and Norway, thanks to favorable electricity prices, renewable energy and a suitable climate. Having the Baltics' first AI factory come here means Estonia is joining the club of countries where the world's leading AI companies are building their infrastructure," Salo said.

In late July, Greenergy Data Centers' Head of Hyperscale Martin Rungi told ERR that attracting one major international customer to Estonia would make it significantly easier for data centers to secure additional customers, as the market develops after the first breakthrough.

In Nebius' case, however, the question of its ties to Russian technology company Yandex cannot be overlooked, as Nebius emerged after Yandex came under sanctions following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

In 2024, the company sold its Russian business units and changed its name to Nebius Group, which is headquartered in the Netherlands. Nebius CEO Arkady Volozh is also a co-founder of Yandex, but has since renounced his Russian citizenship.

A Greenergy representative said last month that such labeling was inappropriate, arguing that Nebius is probably one of the most thoroughly vetted organizations, given that despite its former ties to Russia, it has earned the trust of Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, the U.S. government and the New York Stock Exchange.

Economy minister: We have consulted security agencies

As government agencies have had concerns about Nebius and the workforce at the AI factory set to operate in Hüüru, Estonian security agencies have been consulted, Minister of Economic Affairs and Industry Erkki Keldo said.

"On the one hand, cutting-edge investments like these /.../ are certainly very welcome in Estonia, but on the other hand, the government has an obligation to look at the broader security picture. So yes, we are aware of the background, we are also in contact with Estonian authorities and will certainly minimize the risks," he said, adding that it is very important to understand that the factory is purely a private investment.

If questions arise about a company's background or workforce, there are rules and security agencies in place, and those agencies have also informed the public about potential risks and threats, the minister noted.

"We certainly have to ensure that any sensitive data, sensitive sectors and sensitive technologies do not, for example, fall into the hands of high-risk countries. And when using different types of data, we have to pay attention to whose technology we are using and where we use and store data, to ensure that it is protected. That is certainly what we are doing," Keldo said.

According to Keldo, Nebius was also discussed at a Cabinet meeting on Thursday and discussions on the matter will continue in the coming weeks.

"Estonian businesses need to understand these potential risks, including the company itself and that people with Russian backgrounds and Russian contacts are not welcomed here with overly open arms. We are certainly somewhat more vigilant about this than perhaps other European countries are, and that will remain the case in the future," Keldo said.

The article was updated to add comments from Minister Erkki Keldo.

World.title: Gallery: Tallinn's TV Tower exhibition spotlights Estonian-German ties
World.content:
A new bilingual exhibition at the Tallinn TV Tower explores Estonia's cultural ties with Germany through the personal stories of several prominent Estonians.

"One Language — Many Stories," which opened August 11, features photos and stories about the connections Estonians such as composer Arvo Pärt, neuroscientist Jaan Aru, Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise and former Narva mayor Katri Raik have with Germany and the German language.

The traveling exhibition is part of the TV Tower's celebration of the 35th anniversary of the restoration of Estonian independence as well as the August 1991 events when the tower was defended from Soviet forces, becoming an important symbol of resistance.

Estonia and Germany also restored formal diplomatic relations on August 28, 1991, making the anniversary a shared milestone.

Tallinn TV Tower Foundation board member Kertu Saks noted that over the past 35 years of regained independence, Estonia has maintained close ties with the rest of the world, on both the state and interpersonal levels.

"We often underestimate the role that personal connections in culture, education and business can play in relations between countries," she said. "This exhibition is about those connections, and the deep respect they can foster for another country's culture and language."

The exhibition was created by the German Embassy in Tallinn, with texts by Kirstel Trell and photography by Christian Gogolin and Iris Kivisalu.

World.title: Estonia's State Fleet takes delivery of cutting-edge cow dung-powered vessel
World.content:
Estonia's State Fleet took delivery Wednesday of a new €22 million compressed biomethane vessel to be used to install navigational aids, conduct research and respond to marine pollution.

In fact, it could be said that Estonia has a new Kratt as of Thursday. That is the name given to the State Fleet's new multifunctional work vessel at Baltic Workboats' shipyard in Nasva. The unique vessel, powered by renewable biomethane, is technologically ahead of the global state of the art and could become an export product featuring technology developed in Estonia.

"The State Fleet's task is also to show the market which technologies are reliable and which can be used in the maritime sector. I think that is our role. It is equally important for us to demonstrate that fuel production has a future in Estonia, and this vessel is a perfect example of that. Compressed biomethane has proven itself on land, but not yet at sea. Our job is to serve as something of a testing ground while also showing the market where technology can go," State Fleet Director General Andres Laasma said.

"I think that both Estonia as a country and Baltic Workboats have once again proven that we can develop and build complex projects, and that we can sell this vessel in Norway and anywhere else in the world where green solutions are a priority," Baltic Workboats CEO Margus Vanaselja said.

One of the vessel's captains, who has effectively held the position on land and alongside the quay for the past year, is now eager to get out to sea.

"I've previously done buoy work aboard the Sektor, a buoy tender that is more than 30 years old. This vessel definitely has many more amenities, is much more technologically advanced and is something Estonia needs. It will make our work considerably easier," Kratt captain Sander Laus said.

"On August 12, a naming ceremony was held for a very important vessel. It is the latest innovation from Estonia's marine engineers. The vessel runs on alternative fuels — methane gas extracted from cow manure and electricity," said shipping enthusiast and Kratt spokesperson Marko Matvere.

According to Matvere, the fuel should be slightly cheaper than diesel, which is part of the point, as ships consume large amounts of fuel and place a considerable burden on the environment. "What could be more ingenious than taking literal crap and using it to run an engine? To me, that's the height of innovation," Matvere said with a smile.

While the State Fleet's previous vessel was completed eight years ago, the next new ferry serving Estonia's major islands is expected to be completed in two years. It, too, will use an alternative energy source: electricity.

World.title: Number of MPs backing Ülle Madise as Estonia's next president rises to 62
World.content:
Sixty-two MPs have signed in favor of Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise as a candidate at next month's presidential elections, up from the 55 received as of yesterday.

While 21 signatures are required to nominate a candidate during the registration process next week, the 62 in favor received at the time of writing is only six votes short of the 68 votes needed to get the next head of state elected at the Riigikogu.

Madise, who has not yet publicly given her consent to run, was backed by 61 coalition MPs from the Reform and Eesti 200 parties, plus MPs from the opposition Social Democrats (SDE).

This is not quite a clean sweep of all members of those parties — three MPs had yet to give their signatures: Mart Võrklaev, Margit Sutrop (both Reform) and Züleyxa Izmailova (SDE) were yet to sign in favor of Madise at the time of writing.

Võrklaev told ERR that he was still weighing up the matter. "For now, I would prefer to keep those reasons to myself," he said when asked why he had not yet signed in Madise's favor, and mentioned Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech) rector Tiit Land as an alternative potential candidate. The Reform Party is to meet with Madise next Tuesday.

Mart Võrklaev Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

In response to ERR's inquiry about whether or not she plans to sign her support signature in the near future, Izmailova also said she will decide on giving her signature to Madise, or not, following a meeting between Madise and the SDE Riigikogu faction set for Monday.

Following departures from parties and their Riigikogu groups, the current Riigikogu has a large number of independent MPs, now 20, none of whom have given their signature in favor of Madise yet.

Some have declared that they will not vote at all, while others have promised to form their position after meeting Land and Madise.

The two newest independent MPs, Kalev Stoicescu and Meelis Kiili, who at the start of this week left Eesti 200 and Reform respectively, have stated they may instead back Land, in the interests of providing a choice and a debate, though Stoicescu added that this would not necessarily mean withdrawing his support for Madise.

As a reminder, as recently as July 23, Stoicescu wrote on his social media account that he was awaiting Madise's consent to run and for the collection of signatures in support of her nomination, and that he would back her.

Isamaa (eight seats) and the Center Party (seven seats) have both said they would potentially sign in favor of Land as a candidate, but they are also due to meet Madise too, and will make their decision after that meeting. With 15 seats combined, however, they lack the number of signatures to nominate Land or any other candidate alone, even if the four independent MPs who vote with those parties are factored in — though Stoicescu and Kiili would hold the balance then and could provide the required 21.

Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

The actual nomination process is open Friday, August 21, the day after the Restoration of Independence Day, and runs to Monday, August 24. The Riigikogu voting takes place Wednesday, September 2 and Thursday, September 3.

Madise's name has been mentioned in connection with a potential presidential bid since the start of July. She would likely need to rescind her role as justice chancellor before running for president, due to conflict of interest issues.

World.title: Expert urges people to keep expectations low in the garden
World.content:
Eva Luigas says that she failed this year with growing zucchini and her outdoor cucumbers also struggled, but her tomatoes did very well.

Luigas said the most important thing in gardening is not putting too much pressure on yourself, because everything should be done with joy and curiosity.

"This year I failed at growing zucchini. I have three plant varieties that have produced only female flowers. So I have to go buy zucchini to make soup," said rural lifestyle journal Maakodu managing editor and gardening expert Eva Luigas. "My outdoor cucumbers also struggled this year."

Luigas said she took especially good care of her tomatoes. "I am very excited about the Estonian tomato variety 'Siive.' I sowed the seed on April 11, planted it outside in June, and on August 5 I got my first outdoor tomatoes without any covering," she said.

"The most important thing in gardening is not putting too much pressure on yourself. You cannot do everything anyway. Do not set demands too high. Everything should be done with joy and curiosity," the gardening expert said with a smirk.

In August, she said, you should collect your own seeds and look around to see who has good peas, cucumbers or tomatoes. Perennial beds should be tidied, and garlic should be lifted from the ground, otherwise the cloves will separate. "I even plan to prune apple trees a little," Luigas said. "Summer pruning is also done when you have made a hard cutback in spring."

Luigas also tidies garden edges in August. "At the beginning of August you start applying fall fertilizer. It is a very good time for planting and propagation, a good time to sow something edible again — lettuce, dill and radish. If you do not have free space, then sow for pre‑growing. Just put them in pots and later place them in free spots," Luigas advised.

Knowing a plant variety, she said, gives information about its different characteristics — growth, height, fruit and flower color, flowering and germination time. "It is not hard to keep the seed packets and write things down somewhere. Today you can take a picture with your phone right away," the expert said. "A gardener's life is full of excitement."

World.title: Moby on Tallinn, punk roots, veganism and why he gives music away for free
World.content:
US musician and songwriter Moby gave a wide-ranging interview to ERR while in Estonia as part of a recent tour.

Moby, real name Richard Melville Hall, played the Song Festival Grounds in Tartu earlier this month, as part of a tour marking the 25th anniversary of his seminal album "Play."

Speaking to "Ringvaade," Moby, who had last toured 15 years ago, said his previous visit to Estonia had consisted of "the hotel, the venue, the airport – and that was it." This time, he's been able to walk around, and noted the cooler weather as a relief after 40-degree or more heat in Spain and even England and Denmark.

"The Future Wet" even includes a track "Tallinn," which he said was inspired by Arvo Pärt – "the simplicity, sort of like some of his later simple, meditative work." Moby also noted he and Pärt share a birthday.

His musical journey included a stint studying jazz fusion at nine but he switched track after hearing British punk legends The Clash at age 12. "I don't want to play virtuosic guitar solos. All I want to do is play in a punk rock band and yell at the top of my lungs." He said he's never seen a reason to stick to one genre, citing John Lennon, David Bowie and Joe Strummer as among his influences.

He said he once expected to become a philosophy professor, not a musician. "I thought my whole life was going to be teaching and making music that everyone ignored."

A track of Moby's, "Extreme Ways," appearing in the end credits of the Jason Bourne movies was "a happy accident," he noted, while looking ahead, the musician said he gravitates toward orchestral classical music. "Giving up loud dance music and concerts... and just writing simple quiet classical music... that seems like paradise."

The interview also brought confirmation that Moby is related to Herman Melville (1819–1891), author of "Moby Dick," though he was given the nickname by his father when he was a baby. Ironically given the novel primarily concerns whale hunting, Moby is also well-known for being a champion of animal rights and a vegan for almost four decades now, also touched on in the interview.

World.title: Senior Iraqi security delegation heads to Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A high-level Iraqi security delegation will travel to Riyadh on Thursday, August 13, 2026, to conduct talks regarding recent cross-border drone strikes targeting petroleum infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, according to a senior government source.

The delegation will be led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari, Director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, alongside Iraqi National Intelligence Service (INIS) Chief Hamid Al-Shatri. The trip follows a reciprocal visit to Baghdad days earlier by Saudi Intelligence Chief Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan.

Key Security & Diplomatic Developments

High-Level Delegation: Led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari and Intelligence Chief Hamid Al-Shatri to establish joint intelligence-sharing protocols with Riyadh.

Incident Background: Late last month, the Saudi Ministry of Defense reported intercepting several drones originating from Iraqi territory targeting oil facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh.

Domestic Investigation: Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief Ali Falih al-Zaidi ordered a formal military investigation into the launch origins following the Saudi allegations.

Diplomatic Mediation: The visit comes after international and regional mediation restored diplomatic channels following the cancellation of Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s planned trip to Riyadh late last month amid joint U.S.-Saudi strikes inside Iraq.

Regional Position: During a recent bilateral meeting in Amman between Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, Riyadh reaffirmed support for Iraq while stressing the necessity that Iraqi territory not be utilized as a platform for aggression against neighboring states.

The bilateral security summit aims to reinforce radar tracking, anti-drone intelligence sharing, and border surveillance between Baghdad and Riyadh.

While the “Islamic Resistance in Iraq” denied responsibility for the Saudi oil facility strikes, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s administration is taking direct steps to prevent unauthorized non-state launches, safeguard Iraqi sovereignty, and protect diplomatic and economic ties with Riyadh.

World.title: Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan to visit Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — President of the Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Faiq Zidan, is scheduled to conduct an official visit to Syria on Thursday, August 13, 2026, marking a landmark first-of-its-kind judicial mission to Damascus, according to a senior official source.

The high-level visit aims to hold structured talks with Syrian judicial authorities to address shared legal frameworks, cross-border judicial coordination, counter-terrorism extradition agreements, and legal mechanisms regulating bilateral trade corridors.

World.title: Iraq Transport Ministry reports 95% completion of Development Road designs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani met with the Parliamentary Transport and Communications Committee on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, to review execution milestones across strategic infrastructure projects, including the Development Road, the Grand Fao Port, and national rail modernization.

During the executive session, Al-Hasani presented technical updates on the 1,200-kilometer Development Road Project, confirming that primary design phases are near completion, with railway engineering blueprints reaching 95% and highway transit designs at 85%.

Key Operational Metrics & Project Milestones

Development Road Project: Designs for the 1,200 km transit corridor are nearly complete (95% for railway tracks, 85% for highways). The MOU executed with Turkey serves as a preliminary framework with no current financial or legal obligations.

Grand Fao Port: Submerged tunnel construction reached 86% completion, alongside advanced structural work across five main container berths.

Rail Network Modernization: Ministry teams are actively pursuing the rehabilitation of the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia railway corridor extending toward the Syrian border.

Maritime Fleet Mobilization: State maritime companies confirmed readiness to deploy Iraqi vessels to transport crude oil and refined petroleum products to support alternative national export strategies.

Administrative & Executive Actions: Al-Hasani confirmed the suspension of Iraqi Airways’ former Director-General and two deputies following an internal investigative audit.

Legislative Alignment: Agreement reached to draft amendments to Transport Law No. 80 of 1983 and establish a joint parliamentary-executive committee holding weekly meetings to update transport regulations.

The meeting highlights Iraq’s strategy to transform into a central logistics bridge connecting the Gulf to Europe, bypassing maritime transit chokepoints.

By pairing the Grand Fao Port’s advancing infrastructure with overland rail links extending north to Turkey and west through the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia line toward Syria, the Ministry of Transport is laying the groundwork for integrated commercial supply chains across Eurasia.

World.title: MP Abdul Jabbar proposes 145 km pipeline to boost Basra crude to Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Independent MP and Secretary-General of the Fao–Zakho Coalition, Amer Abdul-Jabbar, proposed a plan on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to construct a 145-kilometer oil pipeline link to transport Basra crude north toward Turkey’s Ceyhan terminal.

Abdul-Jabbar stated via social media that the proposed missing link would instantly increase Iraq’s northern export capacity by 150,000 to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd). To avoid drawing on the federal budget during the ongoing liquidity crisis, he advocated launching a “National Volunteer Effort,” utilizing surplus piping from state-owned enterprises alongside logistical backing from private contractors operating under Ministry of Oil contracts.

Key Technical & Strategy Highlights

Proposed Pipeline Link: A 145 km strategic bypass connecting southern oilfields in Basra directly to northern export routes toward the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Capacity Increase: Designed to boost crude export flows by 150,000 to 300,000 bpd, mitigating bottlenecks caused by Persian Gulf shipping disruptions.

Zero-Cost Volunteer Framework: Proposed execution via a “National Volunteer Effort” using inventory audits of unused piping across state firms and private sector contractor support.

Existing Ministry Export Strategy: Complements Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair’s August 9 plan to export 750,000 bpd to Ceyhan via: 450,000 bpd pumped through the Strategic Pipeline after rehabilitating the PS3 pump station in Najaf and K3 in Haditha. 300,000 bpd transported via road tankers (including 200,000 bpd through KAR Group and 100,000 bpd under a secondary contract).

Long-Term Iraqi-Turkish Energy Framework: Ministry of Oil is finalizing a 1-year interim agreement with Ankara, paving the way for a 10- to 20-year strategic partnership involving Turkish BOTAŞ and BP in developing Kirkuk oilfields.

Abdul-Jabbar’s proposal comes as the Ministry of Oil accelerates alternative land-based export channels to bypass the blocked Strait of Hormuz.

Minister Khudair previously confirmed that Iraq’s State Company for Oil Projects (SCOP) and Turkey’s BOTAŞ are actively inspecting and rehabilitating the northern export system to handle between 500,000 and 750,000 bpd. Implementing the 145 km bypass link could offer Baghdad an immediate, low-cost mechanism to restore crude cash flows while long-term pipeline infrastructure is constructed toward Syria and Jordan.

World.title: Meta meets its own ‘tobacco’ moment in court
World.content:
Oakland – With billions of users around the world, Meta will defend itself against allegations of harming children in a new trial in the United States this week, which experts describe as social media’s big tobacco moment.

After a coalition of states sued Meta in 2023 for allegedly designing addictive features for kids in its apps, four states were selected to represent their claims: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey.

Top prosecutors of those states now aim to prove in federal court that Meta deliberately made Facebook and Instagram addictive for children.

Meta “strongly disagrees with these allegations” and is “confident the evidence will show our longstanding commitment to supporting young people,” a spokesperson told AFP, adding that the company has “listened to parents, worked with experts and law enforcement.”

Although it’s not the first lawsuit that seeks to hold a social media company accountable for its impact on mental health and safety, it could become one of the most consequential.

“It really feels like tobacco in the 1990s,” Vincent Joralemon, a director at Berkeley’s Life Sciences Law and Policy Center, told AFP.

While these cases about social media harms revolve around the intersection of technology and addiction, the legal argument in this case against Meta centers on its business practices, just like when the federal government sued tobacco companies around three decades ago, Joralemon said.

By the early 1990s, decades of research showed that tobacco use caused health problems such as cancer, and eventually additional investigations revealed how the industry deliberately downplayed, and even concealed, the harmful impacts of its products.

– ‘Protecting teens’ –

Dozens of US states sued four major tobacco companies, and by 1998, won a landmark settlement agreement which included financial penalties and changes to how products were marketed, particularly to children whom the industry targeted with s featuring cartoon characters, the most famous of which was known as “Joe Camel.”

Jury selection begins today in Oakland, a short drive from San Francisco and opening statements are expected to begin August 18.

Meta was convicted on similar grounds in separate trials held in Los Angeles and New Mexico, with combined damages that approach $1 billion.

In Oakland, the states are demanding a long list of changes to Meta’s apps, in addition to financial penalties as high as $1.4 trillion, close to Meta’s entire market value which hovers around $1.5 trillion.

Despite the eye-popping number, money isn’t Meta’s biggest problem, if it were to lose the case.

“The huge issue here is reputational harm” and being forced to make major changes, Joralemon said.

“Putting a CEO on the witness stand can be quite damning,” as well, he said.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify.

The case could be “the beginning of a broader reckoning” for Meta, Nora Freeman Engstrom told AFP via email. She is a law professor and associate dean at Stanford.

It will be important to see the “gap” between what Meta knew privately and what it disclosed publicly, Engstrom said.

Meta is “confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts,” Meta told AFP last week.

With so many plaintiffs suing Meta and other social media companies, these lawsuits could potentially “go on for decades,” Joralemon said.

In May, Snap, TikTok, YouTube and Meta settled with a school district in Kentucky for $27 million to avoid another trial that was expected to set a precedent for around 1,200 similar lawsuits.

On Monday, a federal appeals court ruled that more than 3,000 additional lawsuits filed against Meta, YouTube-parent Google, Snap and TikTok can proceed.

World.title: Colombia rescuers find woman alive as quake death toll passes 240
World.content:
Pereira – Colombian rescuers pulled a 32-year-old woman alive from the rubble of a collapsed building Tuesday, sparking cheers and applause as exhausted crews raced to find more survivors from the country’s strongest earthquake in a century.

Daniela Largo was carried from the wreckage wrapped in a blue blanket as rescuers embraced and relatives shouted out with joy.

The rescue came as soldiers, firefighters and volunteers searched collapsed buildings across western Colombia after a 7.4-magnitude quake killed at least 241 people and injured more than 1,600.

“We were losing hope and then we received a call,” said her mother Sandra Milena Perez in Pereira.

Perez said a local resident heard cries for help beneath the rubble and joined neighbors in removing debris before professional rescuers arrived.

“Thanks to him, today we’re happy,” she said. “At home her 12-year-old son is waiting for her.”

In Pereira and in Cali, emergency crews used cranes, dogs and heavy machinery to search ruined buildings while volunteers formed human chains to clear debris by hand, hoping to reach people still trapped beneath collapsed structures.

As darkness fell, families prepared to sleep in parks as aftershocks rattled damaged neighborhoods where entire blocks had been reduced to rubble.

The quake overwhelmed parts of the health system, turning the rescue effort into one of Colombia’s largest disaster responses in years.

“The house came down on top of us. I wasn’t able to get out,” said Beatriz Arcos, who was trapped with her husband and mother beneath their collapsed condominium.

“It took about an hour to get us out.” Arcos said she was hospitalized after a concrete block fell on her back. Her husband and mother were also injured.

In Cali, residents armed with picks, shovels and their bare hands joined firefighters in digging through collapsed buildings.

Rescuers stopped every few minutes to call into the rubble and listen for any response.

“We’re doing this with our hands, with gloves” said volunteer Pablo Cesar Ruiz “It’s sad to see time slipping away.”

In Pereira, army units and sniffer dogs combed through twisted concrete and exposed steel.

At one site, a rescue squad leader abruptly raised his fist, stopping workers so they could listen for signs of life.

Volunteers formed human chains, passing bricks and chunks of masonry hand-to-hand to clear paths into collapsed structures.

– ‘So much effort’ –

For many families, the desperate search was becoming a vigil.

“My aunt lived there. She’s under the rubble,” said Jorge Gonzalez, standing beside a collapsed building in Pereira.

“I arrived yesterday and I haven’t left, and until they find her body I don’t intend to leave here.”

While some families waited for news of missing relatives, others were grappling with the loss of homes, possessions and livelihoods.

“We lost everything,” said Stella Galvis, fighting back tears after escaping the collapse of her home.

“We survived by a miracle, since I managed to get my little boy out and my partner managed to get out too.”

From the air, neighborhoods in Cali appeared flattened, with piles of grey rubble replacing entire blocks of homes and apartment buildings.

Nearby, cars lay crushed beneath fallen walls and concrete slabs.

On one mound of debris, a young couple climbed over broken masonry searching for belongings.

They recovered a box from inside a child’s bright red bedside table.

Many survivors spent the night outdoors, either because their homes were damaged or because they feared aftershocks.

One park in Pereira was transformed into a makeshift shelter with tents and mattresses.

“We lost everything, but we’re alive,” said 23-year-old John Tabasco, who was camped there with his wife and seven-month-old son.

“We’ve never had to do this before, to depend on someone else to help us. It’s amazing how life can change.”

Others struggled to come to terms with losing homes built over decades.

“You buy a little house with so much effort, spending 40, 50 years struggling to get yourself that house, you finally get it and in just a few days it all goes down the drain,” said 79-year-old Jaime Alzate.

In Cali, part of the Hospital Universitario del Valle collapsed during the quake, forcing doctors to move patients into a parking lot and treat some in the open air.

Yet amid the destruction, many Colombians mobilized to help.

Thousands brought water, food and supplies to affected neighborhoods, while long lines formed outside blood donation centers.

“It’s about wanting to help your community, your city and your country,” said blood donor Ferney Cabrera.

President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency and promised rent subsidies for affected families Tuesday during a visit to Pereira.

The United States announced $15.5 million in emergency aid, while messages of support and offers of assistance arrived from around the world.

As aftershocks continued to rattle damaged cities, rescue crews pressed on through the ruins, hoping more voices, taps or whistles might still emerge.

World.title: Passengers rescued as second ferry in days catches fire in Indonesia
World.content:
Mataram – A navy vessel and other ships rushed in Wednesday to rescue over 100 people from a ferry on fire off the tourist island of Bali, officials said, in the second such incident in days.

There were no immediate reports of casualties among the passengers and crew, with at least 114 people on board, according to the manifest.

The passenger ferry had been sailing from Bali to the next-door island of Lombok when it caught fire in the early morning hours.

Muhamad Hariyadi, head of the search and rescue agency at Mataram on Lombok island, said the total number of passengers on board was being verified.

He said passengers were evacuated on at least three different vessels, including a navy ship and another ferry.

Search and rescue vessels were at the scene and a helicopter was conducting surveillance from the air.

“As of now, we have not received any report of casualties,” Hariyadi told Metro TV.

“We have approached the ship and confirmed that all passengers are no longer on board,” he added. “We visually see no passengers on the ship.”

Last week, five people died when a ferry caught fire off Java island.

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia — an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that rely heavily on boat connections.

Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.

A ferry transporting more than 70 people sank while sailing near Selayar, a small island south of Sulawesi, last month.

Four bodies were recovered, but the search operation ended with 14 others still officially missing.

World.title: Charges dropped against Bondi Beach attack hero
World.content:
Sydney – Australian police dropped assault charges on Wednesday against a man lauded for his bravery during last year’s mass shooting at Bondi Beach.

Fruit seller Ahmed al Ahmed was hailed as a hero after footage showed him disarming a gunman during the December 14 attack, which killed 15 people at a Jewish festival.

Ahmed was earlier this year accused of stalking and assaulting his father, charges he denied.

Both charges were withdrawn after a brief hearing on Wednesday, court documents showed.

Ahmed ducked between parked cars as the Bondi shooting unfolded, grabbing one of the two gunmen and wresting away his weapon in an effort to stop the killing.

He sustained gunshot wounds in the attack.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese would later meet Ahmed in person, describing him as a “true Australian hero” and an inspiration to all.

World.title: Bengal govt strips BJP MP Ananta Maharaj of Banga Bibhushan award over 'insulting' remarks against Netaji
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The West Bengal government on Thursday withdrew the Banga Bibhushan award from BJP Rajya Sabha member Ananta Maharaj over his alleged derogatory comment against Netaji.

Banga Bibhushan is one of West Bengalâs highest civilian honours, awarded by the state government to eminent personalities for outstanding contributions in fields such as art, culture, literature, social service and other areas. Speaking at a meeting in Dinhata on July 19, Roy asked, âDid Netaji have the capacity to organise and form the Azad Hind Fauj?â He then claimed that âthey were all British soldiersâ and alleged that âthe Indian National Army (INA) was misused.â

Roy also claimed that the Azad Hind Fauj originated from British-Indian troops who had been handed over by Germany.





His remarks triggered a backlash in West Bengal, with political leaders and Rajbanshi organisations condemning the comments and demanding action against the BJP MP. Prominent Rajbanshi figures issued a joint statement condemning the remarks as false, insulting and damaging to social harmony. Forward Bloc, a party founded by Netaji, also lodged police complaints and demanded the immediate revocation of his Rajya Sabha membership.

World.title: 'This is your last chance': SC ultimatum to Centre over delay in front-of-pack food warning labels
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday sharply criticised the Centre and the

(

) over the delay in introducing front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products high in sugar, salt and saturated fat, warning that it would issue directions if the government failed to take a final decision.

A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran gave the Centre two weeks to place its final decision on record, making it clear that the government could either implement the proposed warning labels on its own or face judicial intervention.

"This is your last chance. Next time we will dictate the judgment," the bench said, according to ANI.

The court repeatedly underlined that the issue was one of public health, particularly the health of children and questioned the government's reluctance to move ahead with stronger nutritional warnings.

"Why? You don't want people of this country to remain healthy? More particularly growing children?" the bench asked during the hearing.

Appearing for the Centre, additional solicitor general Brijender Chahar argued that applying strict warning standards could create complications for traditional Indian food items. He said products such as namkeen could end up carrying red warning symbols because of their fat or salt content.





He also argued that international nutritional standards might not be directly applicable to Indian dietary habits, pointing out that even two eggs could exceed the prescribed daily fat limit.

The court, however, was unconvinced.

The bench said consumers were already aware that packaged foods contained sugar, fat and carbohydrates, but front-of-pack warning labels would provide a simpler and more effective way of communicating nutritional risks before a purchase was made.

The judges also rejected the argument that warning labels could adversely affect manufacturers.

According to ANI, the bench observed that the final decision to purchase a product would continue to rest with consumers and that commercial considerations could not take precedence over public health.

During the proceedings, senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for a manufacturer, attempted to make submissions.

The court responded by stating that the case concerned the health of citizens and that manufacturers could not determine government policy on the issue.

Senior advocate Devadutt Kamat suggested that food products could be categorised differently and that detailed nutritional information should be displayed.

The bench clarified that it was not opposed to any particular food product but was only seeking greater consumer awareness.

"In this country, how many people can afford dry fruits? And how many children buy Kurkure? That makes all the difference. We are not against any particular product. We only want the person purchasing it to know what he is consuming," the court said, according to ANI.

The bench also referred to its February 10, 2026, order, in which it had previously addressed the issue and laid down its observations.

During Thursday's hearing, the petitioner's counsel drew the court's attention to the minutes of an FSSAI meeting held on March 7, which allegedly reflected a position contrary to the suggestions made by the court earlier.

The judges also took exception to the Centre's argument that India could not easily adopt international standards relating to nutritional warnings.

"We do not approve the stance of the Union when it says that it's not possible to match the international standards, more particularly developed countries. Should India remain an undeveloped country?" the bench asked, according to ANI.

"The world should know that India is concerned about the health of its citizens and more particularly children," it added.

The case stems from a petition seeking mandatory front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products containing high levels of sugar, salt and saturated fat.

The proposed labels are intended to help consumers quickly identify potentially unhealthy products before buying them.

World.title: Watch: When gunman tried to assassinate Sukhbir Badal at Golden Temple in 2024
World.content:
On December 4, 2024, Badal was attacked inside the Golden Temple during a penance ordered by the Akal Takht.

NEW DELHI: Sukhbir Singh Badalâs Thursday attack in Nanded marks the second serious attempt on the Shiromani Akali Dal leaderâs life. The SAD leader was also attacked two years ago at the Golden Temple when a gunman opened fire at him while Badal was serving religious punishment at the shrine.On December 4, 2024, Badal was attacked at the entrance of the temple, where he was seated in a wheelchair because of his fractured leg, during a penance ordered by the Akal Takht. Video footage from the incident shows the moment the attacker overpowered him within seconds.The footage showed him dressed in a blue sewadar uniform. He was stationed at the temple entrance as part of the punishment pronounced by the Akal Takht over alleged misconduct during his tenure from 2007 to 2017.As Badal sat with a placard around his neck, a man who was later identified as Narayan Singh Chaura approached him and opened fire. The attempt, however, was foiled almost immediately.In the clip, right after the gunman pulled out the weapon, an alert sewadar, believed to be a volunteer associated with an Akali leader, intervened and pushed the assailantâs arm upward as he attempted to fire. The bullet was discharged harmlessly into the air, and the attacker was quickly overpowered by volunteers and others present at the scene.Police personnel stationed at the shrine also moved in and apprehended Chaura on the spot. Confirming the swift response, ADCP Harpal Singh said, âNo one was injured in the attack.âIt was not long after the attempted attack that other sewadars present at the scene assembled together to create a human shield around Badal.Despite the dramatic shooting attempt, Badal remained calm.Still seated in his wheelchair, he continued performing his duties as a sewadar, holding a spear and staying at the temple entrance after the assailant had been detained.In a separate clip, the shooter could be seen being overpowered by the crowd. The people holding the man can be heard asking him his motive for opening fire on the SAD leader.The religious punishment had been announced on December 2, 2024, by Sikh high priests for Badal and other Akali leaders in connection with incidents of sacrilege and the pardon granted to controversial Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim. The tankhah was part of a reconciliation process led by Sikh religious authorities to address long-standing grievances within the community.With Wednesdayâs attack once again putting security arrangements at the Golden Temple under scrutiny, the earlier firing incident has returned to focus as a reminder that this was not the first time Sukhbir Singh Badal was targeted while performing religious service at Sikhismâs holiest shrine.

Rijiju targets Congress over disruptions

NEW DELHI: Parliamentâs Monsoon Session ended on Thursday with both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha being adjourned sine die, bringing to a close a session marked by repeated disruptions and protests by opposition parties.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the session was successful in terms of legislative business, with 12 Bills passed, but criticised the quality of debates and discussions.Addressing a press briefing, he said the government was not satisfied with the level of parliamentary discussion during the session.Rijiju said Lok Sabha productivity stood at 19% of the total allotted time, while Rajya Sabha recorded 39%.âThe Monsoon Session concluded today. We view it from two perspectives. In terms of business, it was a very successful session; we passed a total of 12 bills. However, from the perspective of debate and discussion, it was not as successful,â Rijiju said.He alleged that opposition parties repeatedly disrupted proceedings and avoided discussions offered by the government.âBased on my parliamentary experience and what I have seen in my life, this is the first time the Opposition was running away from discussions,â he said.According to Rijiju, 11 Bills were passed in the Lok Sabha without discussion, while one Bill underwent discussion. He said the Bills were discussed in the Rajya Sabha, although Congress and some other Opposition members staged a walkout.Rijiju said the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill was the only legislation to undergo a full discussion in the Lok Sabha during the session.âOnly one bill, addressing the issue of paper leaks and unfair means in examinations, underwent a full discussion in the Lok Sabha,â he said.The legislation, which seeks to prevent unfair means in public examinations, was also discussed in the Rajya Sabha before being passed during the session.The Monsoon Session, which began on July 20, witnessed prolonged disruptions in both Houses.Opposition protests initially focused on the NEET paper leak and alleged irregularities involving donations to the Ram temple in Ayodhya.The opposition later sought discussions on police action against students protesting over the NEET issue and demanded statements from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah.The government offered a discussion on the NEET paper leak and related issues, along with a reply from Shah, but the proposal was rejected by the Congress. A similar proposal made on Wednesday also failed to break the deadlock.Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said the Opposition wanted answers over allegations concerning police action against protesting students and criticised the prospect of a speech by Shah.Rijiju accused Congress MPs of reducing their parliamentary role to sloganeering and creating disruptions.âAnother observation I have made is that Congress MPs seem to believe their primary role is merely to raise slogans and create a ruckus with placards and banners,â he said.He also said disruptions had particularly affected newly elected MPs by limiting opportunities for debate and discussion.âAs the minister of parliamentary affairs, I feel genuinely sorry for the Congress MPs, especially the new ones,â Rijiju said. âHow can they learn if there are no debates or discussions?âHe expressed hope that opposition parties would reflect on their conduct and participate in more substantive debates when Parliament reconvenes for the Winter Session.The session also saw counter-protests between BJP and INDIA bloc MPs at the Makar Dwar steps of the Parliament complex.

World.title: 'Bid to weaken stir': Students accuse Jharkhand govt of withholding Devendra Mahto's health details
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who is on an indefinite hunger strike over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand recruitment examinations, remains hospitalised at Sadar Hospital in Ranchi, with protesting students alleging that the state government is withholding information about his health to weaken their agitation.

Meanwhile, former Jharkhand chief minister Raghubar Das on Thursday visited Mahto at the hospital and enquired about his health.

Mahto has been on hunger strike for 11 days and is undergoing treatment after he was injured during a police lathi-charge on August 10. The wider protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants entered its 20th day on Thursday, with students continuing their agitation at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.

Students allege govt hiding Mahtoâs health details

The protesting students have alleged that the government is not allowing them to meet Mahto at the hospital and is withholding details about his health.

Mahto was moved to Sadar Hospital by the administration late Monday evening after police used force to disperse thousands of aspirants who had marched towards the state assembly.

Raghubar Das meets Mahto

In a post on X, Mahto said: "Former Chief Minister of Jharkhand Raghubar Das ji reached the hospital and inquired about my well-being, while also assuring support for our movement."

Das had on Wednesday threatened to go on a hunger strike if the demand for a CBI probe was not fulfilled within a week.





He has also sought compensation of Rs 1 crore each for the families of 19 people who died during the 2024 excise constable physical examination.

The BJP has accused the Hemant Soren government of suppressing the student movement, while the Congress has accused the saffron party of politicising the agitation and alleged that it brought workers from outside Jharkhand to disrupt the protests.

On Tuesday, in a message shared on social media, Mahto said "My body is undergoing treatment in the hospital bed, but my soul and resolve are at the Satyagraha site where students and youth are engaged in a just struggle for their future.

The indefinite hunger strike continues on its 11th day in Sadar Hospital."

Mahto has also sought permission from the hospital authorities to return to the protest site. In a handwritten application to the Civil Surgeon, he said being separated from the protesting students was causing him greater distress than his physical ailments.

He cited his responsibility towards thousands of students protesting against alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations and sought permission to rejoin them.

The protesters have been demanding cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process. They have alleged that their demands have not been fully accepted by the state government.

Jharkhand protest enters 20th day

The studentsâ agitation over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations entered its 20th day on Thursday. The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch has been demonstrating at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, demanding greater transparency in recruitment examinations, cancellation of several tests and an independent probe by the CBI or a panel of retired judges from outside Jharkhand.

Tensions escalated on Monday when JPSC and JSSC aspirants marched towards the state assembly. Police used batons, water cannons and tear gas to disperse the protesters.

Mahto was among those taken to hospital after the confrontation. He later sought permission to leave the hospital and return to the protest site, saying his presence with the students was important to the movement.

The ABVP has announced protests at more than 1,200 universities over the issue. Its leaders have also questioned the credibility of the state-appointed SIT into the alleged examination irregularities, citing repeated changes in its composition.

The protesters have so far refused to call off the agitation, maintaining that they will continue the movement until their demands are addressed.

World.title: UP Creators Summit & Awards to celebrate the state's rising digital voices and creator economy in grand 2-day event
World.content:
As India's creator economy continues to redefine entertainment, entrepreneurship and storytelling, Uttar Pradesh is emerging as one of the country's fastest-growing hubs for digital innovation.

With increasing internet penetration, a thriving startup ecosystem and the rapid rise of creators from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, the state is playing a pivotal role in shaping India's digital future.

Celebrating this transformation, the inaugural edition Times of Indiaâs UP Creators Summit & Awards will bring together some of the state's most influential content creators, industry leaders, brands and digital innovators for a 2-day mega showcase of recognition, insightful conversations and future-focused learning.

To be held on August 19 and 20 in Varanasi, the spiritual and cultural heart of Uttar Pradesh, the event will bring together the stateâs rich heritage and its new-age digital voices, showcasing how creators are shaping the narrative of a new Uttar Pradesh. The first day, August 19, will feature insightful masterclasses, panel discussions and fireside chats, while August 20 will culminate in the grand UP Creators Awards, celebrating the stateâs most impactful digital creators.





Honouring the creators shaping a new Uttar Pradesh

At the heart of the event are the Creators Awards, which will honour creators who are making a meaningful impact across diverse genres, including education, technology, finance, food, travel, lifestyle, comedy, fashion, gaming, social impact and more. These creators are not only building communities online but are also amplifying local stories, inspiring millions and showcasing Uttar Pradesh's talent on the national and global stage.

The awards celebrate creators who are redefining digital influence while contributing to the state's growing reputation as a powerhouse of innovation and creativity.

Conversations driving the future of the creator economy

Beyond the awards, the summit will serve as a platform for thought-provoking discussions on the opportunities and challenges shaping the creator ecosystem.

Panel discussions will explore how the creator economy is expanding beyond metropolitan cities into Tier 2 and Tier 3 India, the growing influence of creators in rebranding Uttar Pradesh, and the role of digital storytellers in building the narrative of a new Uttar Pradesh.

The event will also feature engaging fireside chats on themes such as "Storytellers of a New Bharat" and "Beyond Followers", examining how creators are moving beyond metrics to create meaningful impact, influence culture and build sustainable careers.
